/**
   * Attempt to replace the condition of if or hook immediately that is a
   * reference to a name that is assigned immediately before.
   */
Method code:
454 |   private void tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node n) {
455 |     Node next = n.getNext();
456 | 
457 |     // Look for patterns like the following and replace the if-condition with
458 |     // a constant value so it can later be folded:
459 |     //   var a = /a/;
460 |     //   if (a) {foo(a)}
461 |     // or
462 |     //   a = 0;
463 |     //   a ? foo(a) : c;
464 |     // or
465 |     //   a = 0;
466 |     //   a || foo(a);
467 |     // or
468 |     //   a = 0;
469 |     //   a && foo(a)
470 |     //
471 |     // TODO(johnlenz): This would be better handled by control-flow sensitive
472 |     // constant propagation. As the other case that I want to handle is:
473 |     //   i=0; for(;i<0;i++){}
474 |     // as right now nothing facilitates removing a loop like that.
475 |     // This is here simply to remove the cruft left behind goog.userAgent and
476 |     // similar cases.
477 | 
478 |     if (isSimpleAssignment(n) && isConditionalStatement(next)) {
479 |       Node lhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentName(n);
480 | 
481 |       Node condition = getConditionalStatementCondition(next);
482 |       if (NodeUtil.isName(lhsAssign) && NodeUtil.isName(condition)
483 |           && lhsAssign.getString().equals(condition.getString())) {
484 |         Node rhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentValue(n);
485 |         TernaryValue value = NodeUtil.getExpressionBooleanValue(rhsAssign);
486 |         if (value != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
487 |           int replacementConditionNodeType =
488 |             (value.toBoolean(true)) ? Token.TRUE : Token.FALSE;
489 |           condition.getParent().replaceChild(condition,
490 |               new Node(replacementConditionNodeType));
491 |           reportCodeChange();
492 |         }

===== M0024 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeExits(Node,int,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MinimizeExitPoints.java
Original range: 113-204
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempts to minimize the number of explicit exit points in a control
   * structure to take advantage of the implied exit at the end of the
   * structure.  This is accomplished by removing redundant statements, and
   * moving statements following a qualifying IF node into that node.
   * For example:
   *
   * function () {
   *   if (x) return;
   *   else blah();
   *   foo();
   * }
   *
   * becomes:
   *
   * function () {
   *  if (x) ;
   *  else {
   *    blah();
   *    foo();
   *  }
   *
   * @param n The execution node of a parent to inspect.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName If parent is a label the name of the label to look for,
   *   null otherwise.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks within labels.
   */
Method code:
113 |   void tryMinimizeExits(Node n, int exitType, String labelName) {
114 | 
115 |     // Just an 'exit'.
116 |     if (matchingExitNode(n, exitType, labelName)) {
117 |       NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
118 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
119 |       return;
120 |     }
121 | 
122 |     // Just an 'if'.
123 |     if (n.getType() == Token.IF) {
124 |       Node ifBlock = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
125 |       tryMinimizeExits(ifBlock, exitType, labelName);
126 |       Node elseBlock = ifBlock.getNext();
127 |       if (elseBlock != null) {
128 |         tryMinimizeExits(elseBlock, exitType, labelName);
129 |       }
130 |       return;
131 |     }
132 | 
133 |     // Just a 'try/catch/finally'.
134 |     if (n.getType() == Token.TRY) {
135 |       Node tryBlock = n.getFirstChild();
136 |       tryMinimizeExits(tryBlock, exitType, labelName);
137 |       Node allCatchNodes = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(n);
138 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(allCatchNodes)) {
139 |         Preconditions.checkState(allCatchNodes.hasOneChild());
140 |         Node catchNode = allCatchNodes.getFirstChild();
141 |         Node catchCodeBlock = catchNode.getLastChild();
142 |         tryMinimizeExits(catchCodeBlock, exitType, labelName);
143 |       }
144 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(n)) {
145 |         Node finallyBlock = n.getLastChild();
146 |         tryMinimizeExits(finallyBlock, exitType, labelName);
147 |       }
148 |     }
149 | 
150 |     // Just a 'label'.
151 |     if (n.getType() == Token.LABEL) {
152 |       Node labelBlock = n.getLastChild();
153 |       tryMinimizeExits(labelBlock, exitType, labelName);
154 |     }
155 | 
156 |     // TODO(johnlenz): The last case of SWITCH statement?
157 | 
158 |     // The rest assumes a block with at least one child, bail on anything else.
159 |     if (n.getType() != Token.BLOCK || n.getLastChild() == null) {
160 |       return;
161 |     }
162 | 
163 |     // Multiple if-exits can be converted in a single pass.
164 |     // Convert "if (blah) break;  if (blah2) break; other_stmt;" to
165 |     // become "if (blah); else { if (blah2); else { other_stmt; } }"
166 |     // which will get converted to "if (!blah && !blah2) { other_stmt; }".
167 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
168 | 
169 |       // An 'if' block to process below.
170 |       if (c.getType() == Token.IF) {
171 |         Node ifTree = c;
172 |         Node trueBlock, falseBlock;
173 | 
174 |         // First, the true condition block.
175 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
176 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
177 |         tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(trueBlock, falseBlock,
178 |             ifTree, exitType, labelName);
179 | 
180 |         // Now the else block.
181 |         // The if blocks may have changed, get them again.
182 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
183 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
184 |         if (falseBlock != null) {
185 |           tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(falseBlock, trueBlock,
186 |               ifTree, exitType, labelName);
187 |         }
188 |       }
189 | 
190 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
191 |         break;
192 |       }
193 |     }
194 | 
195 |     // Now try to minimize the exits of the last child, if it is removed
196 |     // look at what has become the last child.
197 |     for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getLastChild()) {
198 |       tryMinimizeExits(c, exitType, labelName);
199 |       // If the node is still the last child, we are done.
200 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
201 |         break;
202 |       }
203 |     }
204 |   }

===== M0028 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

122 |   private void overrideDefines(Map<String, DefineInfo> allDefines) {
123 |     boolean changed = false;
124 |     for (Map.Entry<String, DefineInfo> def : allDefines.entrySet()) {
125 |       String defineName = def.getKey();
126 |       DefineInfo info = def.getValue();
127 |       Node inputValue = dominantReplacements.get(defineName);
128 |       Node finalValue = inputValue != null ?
129 |           inputValue : info.getLastValue();
130 |       if (finalValue != info.initialValue) {
131 |         info.initialValueParent.replaceChild(
132 |             info.initialValue, finalValue.cloneTree());
133 |         compiler.addToDebugLog("Overriding @define variable " + defineName);
134 |         changed = changed ||
135 |             finalValue.getType() != info.initialValue.getType() ||
136 |             !finalValue.isEquivalentTo(info.initialValue);
137 |       }
138 |     }
139 | 
140 |     if (changed) {
141 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
142 |     }
143 | 
144 |     Set<String> unusedReplacements = dominantReplacements.keySet();
145 |     unusedReplacements.removeAll(allDefines.keySet());
146 |     unusedReplacements.removeAll(KNOWN_DEFINES);
147 |     for (String unknownDefine : unusedReplacements) {
148 |       compiler.report(JSError.make(UNKNOWN_DEFINE_WARNING, unknownDefine));
149 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessDefines.CollectDefines.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessDefines.java
Original range: 275-359

Method code:
275 |     public  void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
276 |       RefInfo refInfo = allRefInfo.get(n);
277 |       if (refInfo != null) {
278 |         Ref ref = refInfo.ref;
279 |         Name name = refInfo.name;
280 |         String fullName = name.fullName();
281 |         switch (ref.type) {
282 |           case SET_FROM_GLOBAL:
283 |           case SET_FROM_LOCAL:
284 |             Node valParent = getValueParent(ref);
285 |             Node val = valParent.getLastChild();
286 |             if (valParent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN && name.isSimpleName() &&
287 |                 name.declaration == ref) {
288 |               // For defines, it's an error if a simple name is assigned
289 |               // before it's declared
290 |               compiler.report(
291 |                   t.makeError(val, INVALID_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, fullName));
292 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
293 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,
294 |               // but no longer assigned to a value, e.g.,
295 |               // DEF_FOO = 5; // becomes "5;"
296 | 
297 |               // We can't remove the ASSIGN/VAR when we're still visiting its
298 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.
299 |               refInfo.name.removeRef(ref);
300 |               lvalueToRemoveLater = valParent;
301 |             }
302 |             break;
303 |           default:
304 |             if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
305 |               // Treat this as a reference to a define in the global scope.
306 |               // After this point, the define must not be reassigned,
307 |               // or it's an error.
308 |               DefineInfo info = assignableDefines.get(fullName);
309 |               if (info != null) {
310 |                 setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
311 |                 assignableDefines.remove(fullName);
312 |               }
313 |             }
314 |             break;
315 |         }
316 |       }
317 | 
318 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope() &&
319 |           n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isDefine()) {
320 |         // warn about @define annotations in local scopes
321 |         compiler.report(
322 |             t.makeError(n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
323 |       }
324 | 
325 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
326 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
327 |         if (n.getType() == Token.ASSIGN) {
328 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
329 |           n.removeChild(last);
330 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
331 |         } else {
332 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() == Token.NAME);
333 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
334 |         }
335 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
336 |       }
337 | 
338 |       if (n.getType() == Token.CALL) {
339 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
340 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
341 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
342 |           //
343 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
344 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
345 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
346 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which
347 |           // are not. But this would be overkill, expecially because
348 |           // the intended use of defines is with config_files, where
349 |           // all the defines are at the top of the bundle.
350 |           for (DefineInfo info : assignableDefines.values()) {
351 |             setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
352 |           }
353 | 
354 |           assignableDefines.clear();
355 |         }
356 |       }
357 | 
358 |       updateAssignAllowedStack(n, false);
359 |     }

52 |   @Override
53 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
54 |     GraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = t.getControlFlowGraph().getNode(n);
55 |     if (gNode != null && gNode.getAnnotation() != GraphReachability.REACHABLE) {
56 | 
57 |       // Only report error when there are some line number informations.
58 |       // There are synthetic nodes with no line number informations, nodes

66 |         // give more warning related to code section reachable from this node.

292 |   static boolean isImmutableValue(Node n) {

===== M0074 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 530-673
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
530 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
531 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
532 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
533 |     // that we know to be safe
534 |     switch (n.getType()) {
535 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
536 |       case Token.AND:
537 |       case Token.BLOCK:
538 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
539 |       case Token.HOOK:
540 |       case Token.IF:
541 |       case Token.IN:
542 |       case Token.LP:
543 |       case Token.NUMBER:
544 |       case Token.OR:
545 |       case Token.THIS:
546 |       case Token.TRUE:
547 |       case Token.FALSE:
548 |       case Token.NULL:
549 |       case Token.STRING:
550 |       case Token.SWITCH:
551 |       case Token.TRY:
552 |       case Token.EMPTY:
553 |         break;
554 | 
555 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
556 |       case Token.THROW:
557 |         return true;
558 | 
559 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
560 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
561 |           return true;
562 |         }
563 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
564 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
565 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
566 |             return true;
567 |           }
568 |         }
569 |         return false;
570 | 
571 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
572 |       case Token.REGEXP:
573 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
574 |           return true;
575 |         }
576 |         break;
577 | 
578 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
579 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
580 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
581 |           return true;
582 |         }
583 |         break;
584 | 
585 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
586 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
587 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
588 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
589 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
590 | 
591 |       case Token.NEW:
592 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
593 |           return true;
594 |         }
595 | 
596 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
597 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
598 |           // side-effects
599 |           break;
600 |         }
601 |         return true;
602 | 
603 |       case Token.CALL:
604 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
605 |         // side effect property set.
606 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
607 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
608 |           // side-effects
609 |           break;
610 |         }
611 |         return true;
612 | 
613 |       default:
614 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
615 |           break;
616 |         }
617 | 
618 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
619 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
620 |           if (isName(assignTarget)) {
621 |             return true;
622 |           }
623 | 
624 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
625 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
626 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
627 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
628 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
629 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
630 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
631 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
632 |             return true;
633 |           }
634 | 
635 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
636 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
637 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
638 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
639 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
640 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
641 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
642 |               return false;
643 |             }
644 | 
645 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
646 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
647 |             // other objects.
648 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
649 |             // side-effect.
650 |             while (isGet(current)) {
651 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
652 |             }
653 | 
654 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
655 |           } else {
656 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
657 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
658 |             // preserve existing behavior.
659 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
660 |           }
661 |         }
662 | 
663 |         return true;
664 |     }
665 | 
666 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
667 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
668 |         return true;
669 |       }
670 |     }
671 | 
672 |     return false;
673 |   }

364 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same

/**
   * Try to fold an array join: ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('') -> 'abc';
   */
Method code:
1154 |   private Node tryFoldArrayJoin(Node n) {
1155 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
1156 | 
1157 |     if (callTarget == null) {
1158 |       return n;
1159 |     }
1160 | 
1161 |     Node right = callTarget.getNext();
1162 | 
1163 |     if (right == null) {
1164 |       return n;
1165 |     }
1166 | 
1167 |     if (!NodeUtil.isGetProp(callTarget) || !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(right)) {
1168 |       return n;
1169 |     }
1170 | 
1171 |     Node arrayNode = callTarget.getFirstChild();
1172 |     Node functionName = arrayNode.getNext();
1173 | 
1174 |     if ((arrayNode.getType() != Token.ARRAYLIT) ||
1175 |         !functionName.getString().equals("join")) {
1176 |       return n;
1177 |     }
1178 | 
1179 |     String joinString = NodeUtil.getStringValue(right);
1180 |     List<Node> arrayFoldedChildren = Lists.newLinkedList();
1181 |     StringBuilder sb = null;
1182 |     int foldedSize = 0;
1183 |     Node prev = null;
1184 |     Node elem = arrayNode.getFirstChild();
1185 |     // Merges adjacent String nodes.
1186 |     while (elem != null) {
1187 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(elem)) {
1188 |         if (sb == null) {
1189 |           sb = new StringBuilder();
1190 |         } else {
1191 |           sb.append(joinString);
1192 |         }
1193 |         sb.append(NodeUtil.getStringValue(elem));
1194 |       } else {
1195 |         if (sb != null) {
1196 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
1197 |           // + 2 for the quotes.
1198 |           foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
1199 |           arrayFoldedChildren.add(
1200 |               Node.newString(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
1201 |           sb = null;
1202 |         }
1203 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(elem);
1204 |         arrayFoldedChildren.add(elem);
1205 |       }
1206 |       prev = elem;
1207 |       elem = elem.getNext();
1208 |     }
1209 | 
1210 |     if (sb != null) {
1211 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
1212 |       // + 2 for the quotes.
1213 |       foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
1214 |       arrayFoldedChildren.add(
1215 |           Node.newString(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
1216 |     }
1217 |     // one for each comma.
1218 |     foldedSize += arrayFoldedChildren.size() - 1;
1219 | 
1220 |     int originalSize = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(n);
1221 |     switch (arrayFoldedChildren.size()) {
1222 |       case 0:
1223 |         Node emptyStringNode = Node.newString("");
1224 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, emptyStringNode);
1225 |         reportCodeChange();
1226 |         return emptyStringNode;
1227 |       case 1:
1228 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
1229 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
1230 |           return n;
1231 |         }
1232 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
1233 |         if (foldedStringNode.getType() != Token.STRING) {
1234 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
1235 |           // it is coerced to a string.
1236 |           Node replacement = new Node(Token.ADD,
1237 |               Node.newString("").copyInformationFrom(right),
1238 |               foldedStringNode);
1239 |           foldedStringNode = replacement;
1240 |         }
1241 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, foldedStringNode);
1242 |         reportCodeChange();
1243 |         return foldedStringNode;
1244 |       default:
1245 |         // No folding could actually be performed.
1246 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
1247 |           return n;
1248 |         }
1249 |         int kJoinOverhead = "[].join()".length();
1250 |         foldedSize += kJoinOverhead;
1251 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(right);
1252 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
1253 |           return n;
1254 |         }
1255 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
1256 |         for (Node node : arrayFoldedChildren) {
1257 |           arrayNode.addChildToBack(node);
1258 |         }
1259 |         reportCodeChange();
1260 |         break;
1261 |     }
1262 | 
1263 |     return n;
1264 |   }

   * Stop the trace.
   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread
   * that started it.
   * @param silence_threshold Traces for time less than silence_threshold
   * ms will be left out of the trace report. A value of -1 indicates
   * that the current ThreadTrace silence_threshold should be used.
   * @return The time that this trace actually ran
   */
Method code:
420 |   long stop(int silence_threshold) {
421 |     Preconditions.checkState(Thread.currentThread() == startThread);
422 |

425 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {

430 |     if (extraTracingValues != null) {

432 |       // a new statistic may have been added
433 |       for (int i = 0; i < extraTracingValues.length; i++) {
434 |         long value = extraTracingStatistics.get(i).stop(startThread);
435 |         extraTracingValues[i] = value - extraTracingValues[i];

441 |       return 0;
442 |     }
443 |

===== M0109 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.computeGenKill(Node,BitSet,BitSet,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 178-263
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the GEN and KILL set.
   *
   * @param n Root node.
   * @param gen Local variables that are live because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param kill Local variables that are killed because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param conditional {@code true} if any assignments encountered are
   *        conditionally executed. These assignments might not kill a variable.
   */
Method code:
178 |   private void computeGenKill(Node n, BitSet gen, BitSet kill,
179 |       boolean conditional) {
180 | 
181 |     switch (n.getType()) {
182 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
183 |       case Token.BLOCK:
184 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
185 |         return;
186 | 
187 |       case Token.WHILE:
188 |       case Token.DO:
189 |       case Token.IF:
190 |         computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
191 |             conditional);
192 |         return;
193 | 
194 |       case Token.FOR:
195 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
196 |           computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
197 |               conditional);
198 |         } else {
199 |           // for(x in y) {...}
200 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
201 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
202 |           if (NodeUtil.isVar(lhs)) {
203 |             // for(var x in y) {...}
204 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild();
205 |           }
206 |           addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
207 |           addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
208 |           computeGenKill(rhs, gen, kill, conditional);
209 |         }
210 |         return;
211 | 
212 |       case Token.VAR:
213 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
214 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
215 |             computeGenKill(c.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
216 |             if (!conditional) {
217 |               addToSetIfLocal(c, kill);
218 |             }
219 |           }
220 |         }
221 |         return;
222 | 
223 |       case Token.AND:
224 |       case Token.OR:
225 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
226 |         // May short circuit.
227 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
228 |         return;
229 | 
230 |       case Token.HOOK:
231 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
232 |         // Assume both sides are conditional.
233 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), gen, kill, true);
234 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
235 |         return;
236 | 
237 |       case Token.NAME:
238 |         if (isArgumentsName(n)) {
239 |           markAllParametersEscaped();
240 |         } else {
241 |           addToSetIfLocal(n, gen);
242 |         }
243 |         return;
244 | 
245 |       default:
246 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isName(n.getFirstChild())) {
247 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
248 |           if (!conditional) {
249 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
250 |           }
251 |           if (!NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
252 |             // assignments such as a += 1 reads a.
253 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
254 |           }
255 |           computeGenKill(lhs.getNext(), gen, kill, conditional);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var,ReferenceCollection)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 635-685
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether the reference collection describes a variable that
     * is initialized to an immutable value, never modified, and defined before
     * every reference.
     */
Method code:
635 |     private boolean isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var v,
636 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
637 |       List<Reference> refSet = refInfo.references;
638 |       int startingReadRef = 1;
639 |       Reference refDecl = refSet.get(0);
640 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(refDecl)) {
641 |         return false;
642 |       }
643 | 
644 |       boolean isNeverAssigned = refInfo.isNeverAssigned();
645 |       // For values that are never assigned, only the references need to be
646 |       // checked.
647 |       if (!isNeverAssigned) {
648 |         Reference refInit = refInfo.getInitializingReference();
649 |         if (!isValidInitialization(refInit)) {
650 |           return false;
651 |         }
652 | 
653 |         if (refDecl != refInit) {
654 |           Preconditions.checkState(refInit == refSet.get(1));
655 |           startingReadRef = 2;
656 |         }
657 | 
658 |         if (!refInfo.isWellDefined()) {
659 |           return false;
660 |         }
661 | 
662 |         Node value = refInit.getAssignedValue();
663 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
664 | 
665 |         boolean isImmutableValueWorthInlining =
666 |             NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value) &&
667 |             (value.getType() != Token.STRING ||
668 |                 isStringWorthInlining(v, refInfo.references));
669 |         boolean isInlinableThisAlias =
670 |             value.getType() == Token.THIS &&
671 |             !refInfo.isEscaped();
672 |         if (!isImmutableValueWorthInlining && !isInlinableThisAlias) {
673 |           return false;
674 |         }
675 |       }
676 | 
677 |       for (int i = startingReadRef; i < refSet.size(); i++) {
678 |         Reference ref = refSet.get(i);
679 |         if (!isValidReference(ref)) {
680 |           return false;
681 |         }
682 |       }
683 | 
684 |       return true;
685 |     }

1071 |   private Node tryFoldKnownStringMethods(Node subtree) {

1075 |     // then dispatch to specific folding method.

1079 |     }

1082 |     if (firstArg == null) {
1083 |       return subtree;
1084 |     }
1085 |

1087 |         !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(firstArg)) {

1089 |     }

1092 |     Node functionName = stringNode.getNext();
1093 | 
1094 |     if ((stringNode.getType() != Token.STRING) || (
1095 |         (functionName.getType() != Token.STRING))) {

1097 |     }

1100 |     if (functionNameString.equals("indexOf") ||
1101 |         functionNameString.equals("lastIndexOf")) {
1102 |       subtree = tryFoldStringIndexOf(subtree, functionNameString,
1103 |           stringNode, firstArg);
1104 |     } else if (functionNameString.equals("substr")) {
1105 |       subtree = tryFoldStringSubstr(subtree, stringNode, firstArg);
1106 |     } else if (functionNameString.equals("substring")) {

   * Compare this node to node2 recursively and return the first pair of nodes

===== M0194 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.inlineNonConstants(Var,ReferenceCollection)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 225-291
Documentation:

Method code:
225 |     private void inlineNonConstants(
226 |         Var v, ReferenceCollection referenceInfo) {
227 |       int refCount = referenceInfo.references.size();
228 |       Reference declaration = referenceInfo.references.get(0);
229 |       Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReference();
230 |       int firstRefAfterInit = (declaration == init) ? 2 : 3;
231 | 
232 |       if (refCount > 1 &&
233 |           isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(v, referenceInfo)) {
234 |         // if the variable is referenced more than once, we can only
235 |         // inline it if it's immutable and never defined before referenced.
236 |         Node value;
237 |         if (init != null) {
238 |           value = init.getAssignedValue();
239 |         } else {
240 |           // Create a new node for variable that is never initialized.
241 |           Node srcLocation = declaration.getNameNode();
242 |           value = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(srcLocation);
243 |         }
244 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
245 |         inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
246 |         staleVars.add(v);
247 |       } else if (refCount == firstRefAfterInit) {
248 |         // The variable likely only read once, try some more
249 |         // complex inlining heuristics.
250 |         Reference reference = referenceInfo.references.get(
251 |             firstRefAfterInit - 1);
252 |         if (canInline(declaration, init, reference)) {
253 |           inline(v, declaration, init, reference);
254 |           staleVars.add(v);
255 |         }
256 |       } else if (declaration != init && refCount == 2) {
257 |         if (isValidDeclaration(declaration) && isValidInitialization(init)) {
258 |           // The only reference is the initialization, remove the assignment and
259 |           // the variable declaration.
260 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
261 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
262 |           inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
263 |           staleVars.add(v);
264 |         }
265 |       }
266 | 
267 |       // If this variable was not inlined normally, check if we can
268 |       // inline an alias of it. (If the variable was inlined, then the
269 |       // reference data is out of sync. We're better off just waiting for
270 |       // the next pass.)
271 |       if (!staleVars.contains(v) && referenceInfo.isWellDefined() &&
272 |           referenceInfo.isAssignedOnceInLifetime()) {
273 |         List<Reference> refs = referenceInfo.references;
274 |         for (int i = 1 /* start from a read */; i < refs.size(); i++) {
275 |           Node nameNode = refs.get(i).getNameNode();
276 |           if (aliasCandidates.containsKey(nameNode)) {
277 |             AliasCandidate candidate = aliasCandidates.get(nameNode);
278 |             if (!staleVars.contains(candidate.alias)) {
279 |               Reference aliasInit;
280 |               aliasInit = candidate.refInfo.getInitializingReference();
281 |               Node value = aliasInit.getAssignedValue();
282 |               Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
283 |               inlineWellDefinedVariable(candidate.alias,
284 |                   value,
285 |                   candidate.refInfo.references);
286 |               staleVars.add(candidate.alias);
287 |             }
288 |           }
289 |         }
290 |       }
291 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.handleStmtList(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 482-521
Documentation:

Method code:
482 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
483 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
484 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
485 |     if (node.getType() == Token.BLOCK && parent != null &&
486 |         parent.getType() == Token.TRY &&
487 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
488 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
489 |       return;
490 |     }
491 | 
492 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
493 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
494 | 
495 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
496 |     // function (unless it is called)
497 |     while (child != null && child.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
498 |       child = child.getNext();
499 |     }
500 | 
501 |     if (child != null) {
502 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
503 |     } else {
504 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node, this));
505 |     }
506 | 
507 |     // Synthetic blocks
508 |     if (parent != null) {
509 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
510 |         case Token.DEFAULT:
511 |         case Token.CASE:
512 |         case Token.TRY:
513 |           break;
514 |         default:
515 |           if (node.getType() == Token.BLOCK && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
516 |             createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFollowNode(node, this));
517 |           }
518 |           break;
519 |       }
520 |     }
521 |   }

   *

1069 |   Node parseInputs() {

1098 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1099 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1100 |           return null;
1101 |         }
1102 |         externsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1103 |       }
1104 | 
1105 |       // Check if the sources need to be re-ordered.
1106 |       if (options.manageClosureDependencies) {
1107 |         for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1108 |           input.setCompiler(this);
1109 | 
1110 |           // Forward-declare all the provided types, so that they
1111 |           // are not flagged even if they are dropped from the process.
1112 |           for (String provide : input.getProvides()) {
1113 |             getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(provide);
1114 |           }
1115 |         }
1116 | 
1117 |         try {
1118 |           inputs =
1119 |               (moduleGraph == null ? new JSModuleGraph(modules) : moduleGraph)
1120 |               .manageDependencies(
1121 |                   options.manageClosureDependenciesEntryPoints, inputs);
1122 |         } catch (CircularDependencyException e) {
1123 |           report(JSError.make(
1124 |               JSModule.CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1125 |           return null;
1126 |         } catch (MissingProvideException e) {
1127 |           report(JSError.make(
1128 |               MISSING_ENTRY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1129 |           return null;
1130 |         }
1131 |       }
1132 | 
1133 |       // Check if inputs need to be rebuilt from modules.
1134 |       boolean staleInputs = false;
1135 |       for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1136 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1137 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1138 |           return null;
1139 |         }
1140 | 
1141 |         // Inputs can have a null AST during initial parse.
1142 |         if (n == null) {
1143 |           continue;
1144 |         }
1145 | 
1146 |         if (n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
1147 |           JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
1148 |           if (info.isExterns()) {
1149 |             // If the input file is explicitly marked as an externs file, then
1150 |             // assume the programmer made a mistake and throw it into
1151 |             // the externs pile anyways.

1174 |         if (n == null) {
1175 |           continue;
1176 |         }
1177 | 
1178 |         if (devMode) {
1179 |           runSanityCheck();

1181 |             return null;
1182 |           }
1183 |         }

1185 |         if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null ||
1186 |             options.nameReferenceReportPath != null) {
1187 |

1189 |           // input file. This information is used to construct the SourceMap.
1190 |           SourceInformationAnnotator sia =
1191 |               new SourceInformationAnnotator(
1192 |                   input.getName(), options.devMode != DevMode.OFF);
1193 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(this, n, sia);
1194 |         }

1197 |       }

1199 |       externAndJsRoot = new Node(Token.BLOCK, externsRoot, jsRoot);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.ReferenceCollection.isWellDefined()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 250-273
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines if the variable for this reference collection is
     * "well-defined." A variable is well-defined if we can prove at
     * compile-time that it's assigned a value before it's used.
     *
     * Notice that if this function returns false, this doesn't imply that the
     * variable is used before it's assigned. It just means that we don't
     * have enough information to make a definitive judgement.
     */
Method code:
250 |     protected boolean isWellDefined() {
251 |       int size = references.size();
252 |       if (size == 0) {
253 |         return false;
254 |       }
255 | 
256 |       // If this is a declaration that does not instantiate the variable,
257 |       // it's not well-defined.
258 |       Reference init = getInitializingReference();
259 |       if (init == null) {
260 |         return false;
261 |       }
262 | 
263 |       Preconditions.checkState(references.get(0).isDeclaration());
264 |       BasicBlock initBlock = init.getBasicBlock();
265 |       for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
266 |         if (!initBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(
267 |                 references.get(i).getBasicBlock())) {
268 |           return false;
269 |         }
270 |       }
271 | 
272 |       return true;
273 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.matchingExitNode(Node,int,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MinimizeExitPoints.java
Original range: 283-298
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if n matches the type and name for the following types of
   * "exits":
   *    - return without values
   *    - continues and breaks with or without names.
   * @param n The node to inspect.
   * @param type The Token type to look for.
   * @param labelName The name that must be associated with the exit type.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks associated with labels.
   * @return Whether the node matches the specified block-exit type.
   */
Method code:
283 |   static private boolean matchingExitNode(Node n, int type, String labelName) {
284 |     if (n.getType() == type) {
285 |       if (type == Token.RETURN) {
286 |         // only returns without expressions.
287 |         return !n.hasChildren();
288 |       } else {
289 |         if (labelName == null) {
290 |           return !n.hasChildren();
291 |         } else {
292 |           return n.hasChildren()
293 |             && labelName.equals(n.getFirstChild().getString());
294 |         }
295 |       }
296 |     }
297 |     return false;
298 |   }

   * Tries to remove n if an unconditional branch node (break, continue or
   * return) if the target of n is the same as the the follow of n. That is, if
   * we remove n, the control flow remains the same. Also if n targets to
   * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to remove
   * the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this removal
   * is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
   *
   * break -> break -> break
   *
   * where all 3 break's are useless. The order of removal matters. When we
   * first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd break.
   * However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes useless and
   * finally the first break becomes useless as well.
   *
   * @return The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
   *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
   */
Method code:
145 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
146 |   private Node tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
147 |     /*
148 |      * For each of the unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
149 |      * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
150 |      * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
151 |      *
152 |      * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
153 |      * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
154 |      * much nicer.
155 |      */
156 | 
157 |     // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
158 |     if (n == null) {
159 |        return n;
160 |     }
161 | 
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = curCfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
163 | 
164 |     if (gNode == null) {
165 |       return n;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     // If the parent is null, this mean whatever node it was there is now
169 |     // useless and it has been removed by other logics in this pass. That node
170 |     // while no longer exists in the AST, is still in the CFG because we
171 |     // never update the graph as nodes are removed.
172 |     if (n.getParent() == null) {
173 |       List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
174 |       if (outEdges.size() == 1) {
175 |         return tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(
176 |           outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue());
177 |       }
178 |     }
179 | 
180 |     switch (n.getType()) {
181 |       case Token.BLOCK:
182 |         if (n.hasChildren()) {
183 |           Node first = n.getFirstChild();
184 |           return tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(first);
185 |         } else {
186 |           return tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(
187 |             ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(n));
188 |         }
189 |       case Token.RETURN:
190 |         if (n.hasChildren()) {
191 |           break;
192 |         }
193 |       case Token.BREAK:
194 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
195 | 
196 |         // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
197 |         // branches to the same node. If removing it the control flow still
198 |         // branches to that same node. It is safe to remove it.
199 |         List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
200 |         if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
201 | 
202 |             // If there is a next node, there is no chance this jump is useless.
203 |             (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().getType() == Token.FUNCTION)) {
204 |           Preconditions.checkState(outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
205 |           Node fallThrough = tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(
206 |             ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(n));
207 |           Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
208 |           if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
209 |             removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n);
210 |             return fallThrough;
211 |           }
212 | 
213 |         }
214 |     }
215 |     return n;
216 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }

/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1570 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1571 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1572 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1573 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1574 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1575 |       // {?} - right curly
1576 |       // {?=} - equals
1577 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1578 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1579 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1580 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1581 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1582 |       token = next();
1583 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1584 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1585 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1586 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1587 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1588 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1589 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1590 |       }
1591 | 
1592 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1593 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1594 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1595 |     } else {
1596 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1597 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1598 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1599 |           next();
1600 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1601 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1602 |           next();
1603 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1604 |         }
1605 |       }
1606 | 
1607 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1608 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.AbstractCommandLineRunner.processResults(Result,List<JSModule>,B)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AbstractCommandLineRunner.java
Original range: 598-707
Documentation:
/**
   * Processes the results of the compile job, and returns an error code.
   */
Method code:
598 |   int processResults(Result result, List<JSModule> modules, B options)
599 |        throws FlagUsageException, IOException {
600 |     if (config.computePhaseOrdering) {
601 |       return 0;
602 |     }
603 | 
604 |     if (config.printPassGraph) {
605 |       if (compiler.getRoot() == null) {
606 |         return 1;
607 |       } else {
608 |         out.append(DotFormatter.toDot(compiler.getPassConfig().getPassGraph()));
609 |         out.append('\n');
610 |         return 0;
611 |       }
612 |     }
613 | 
614 |     if (config.printAst) {
615 |       if (compiler.getRoot() == null) {
616 |         return 1;
617 |       } else {
618 |         ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg = compiler.computeCFG();
619 |         DotFormatter.appendDot(compiler.getRoot().getLastChild(), cfg, out);
620 |         out.append('\n');
621 |         return 0;
622 |       }
623 |     }
624 | 
625 |     if (config.printTree) {
626 |       if (compiler.getRoot() == null) {
627 |         out.append("Code contains errors; no tree was generated.\n");
628 |         return 1;
629 |       } else {
630 |         compiler.getRoot().appendStringTree(out);
631 |         out.append("\n");
632 |         return 0;
633 |       }
634 |     }
635 | 
636 |     if (result.success) {
637 |       if (modules == null) {
638 |         writeOutput(out, compiler, compiler.toSource(), config.outputWrapper,
639 |             config.outputWrapperMarker);
640 | 
641 |         // Output the source map if requested.
642 |         outputSourceMap(options);
643 |       } else {
644 |         String moduleFilePrefix = config.moduleOutputPathPrefix;
645 |         maybeCreateDirsForPath(moduleFilePrefix);
646 |         Map<String, String> moduleWrappers =
647 |             parseModuleWrappers(config.moduleWrapper, modules);
648 | 
649 |         // If the source map path is in fact a pattern for each
650 |         // module, create a stream per-module. Otherwise, create
651 |         // a single source map.
652 |         Writer mapOut = null;
653 | 
654 |         if (!shouldGenerateMapPerModule(options)) {
655 |           mapOut = fileNameToOutputWriter(expandSourceMapPath(options, null));
656 |         }
657 | 
658 |         for (JSModule m : modules) {
659 |           if (shouldGenerateMapPerModule(options)) {
660 |             mapOut = fileNameToOutputWriter(expandSourceMapPath(options, m));
661 |           }
662 | 
663 |           Writer writer = fileNameToOutputWriter(
664 |               moduleFilePrefix + m.getName() + ".js");
665 | 
666 |           if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null) {
667 |             compiler.getSourceMap().reset();
668 |           }
669 | 
670 |           writeOutput(writer, compiler, compiler.toSource(m), moduleWrappers.get(
671 |               m.getName()), "%s");
672 | 
673 |           if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null) {
674 |             compiler.getSourceMap().appendTo(mapOut, m.getName());
675 |           }
676 | 
677 |           writer.close();
678 | 
679 |           if (shouldGenerateMapPerModule(options) && mapOut != null) {
680 |             mapOut.close();
681 |             mapOut = null;
682 |           }
683 |         }
684 | 
685 |         if (mapOut != null) {
686 |           mapOut.close();
687 |         }
688 |       }
689 | 
690 |       // Output the externs if required.
691 |       if (options.externExportsPath != null) {
692 |         Writer eeOut =
693 |             openExternExportsStream(options, options.jsOutputFile);
694 |         eeOut.append(result.externExport);
695 |         eeOut.close();
696 |       }
697 | 
698 |       // Output the variable and property name maps if requested.
699 |       outputNameMaps(options);
700 | 
701 |       // Output the manifest if requested.
702 |       outputManifest();
703 |     }
704 | 
705 |     // return 0 if no errors, the error count otherwise
706 |     return Math.min(result.errors.length, 0x7f);
707 |   }

Original range: 1515-1517
Documentation:
/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1515 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1516 |     return n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION && !isStatement(n);
1517 |   }

===== M0309 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseVariableDeclarations.GatherCollapses.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseVariableDeclarations.java
Original range: 348-377
Documentation:

Method code:
348 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
349 |       // Only care about var nodes
350 |       if (n.getType() != Token.VAR) return;
351 | 
352 |       // If we've already looked at this node, skip it
353 |       if (nodesToCollapse.contains(n)) return;
354 | 
355 |       // Adjacent VAR children of an IF node are the if and else parts and can't
356 |       // be collapsed
357 |       if (parent.getType() == Token.IF) return;
358 | 
359 |       Node varNode = n;
360 | 
361 |       // Find variable declarations that follow this one (if any)
362 |       n = n.getNext();
363 | 
364 |       boolean hasNodesToCollapse = false;
365 |       while (n != null && n.getType() == Token.VAR) {
366 |         nodesToCollapse.add(n);
367 |         hasNodesToCollapse = true;
368 | 
369 |         n = n.getNext();
370 |       }
371 | 
372 |       if (hasNodesToCollapse) {
373 |         nodesToCollapse.add(varNode);
374 |         collapses.add(new Collapse(varNode, parent));
375 |       }
376 | 
377 |     }

===== M0318 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

===== M0322 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.AbstractCommandLineRunner.createDefineReplacements(List<String>,CompilerOptions)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AbstractCommandLineRunner.java
Original range: 989-1038
Documentation:
/**
   * Create a map of constant names to constant values from a textual
   * description of the map.
   *
   * @param definitions A list of overriding definitions for defines in
   *     the form <name>[=<val>], where <val> is a number, boolean, or
   *     single-quoted string without single quotes.
   */
Method code:
989 |   @VisibleForTesting
990 |   static void createDefineReplacements(List<String> definitions,
991 |       CompilerOptions options) {
992 |     // Parse the definitions
993 |     for (String override : definitions) {
994 |       String[] assignment = override.split("=", 2);
995 |       String defName = assignment[0];
996 | 
997 |       if (defName.length() > 0) {
998 |         if (assignment.length == 1) {
999 |           options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, true);
1000 |           continue;
1001 |         } else {
1002 |           String defValue = assignment[1];
1003 | 
1004 |           if (defValue.equals("true")) {
1005 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, true);
1006 |             continue;
1007 |           } else if (defValue.equals("false")) {
1008 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, false);
1009 |             continue;
1010 |           } else if (defValue.length() > 1
1011 |               && ((defValue.charAt(0) == '\'' &&
1012 |                   defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\'')
1013 |                   || (defValue.charAt(0) == '\"' &&
1014 |                       defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\"'))) {
1015 |             // If the value starts and ends with a single quote,
1016 |             // we assume that it's a string.
1017 |             String maybeStringVal =
1018 |                 defValue.substring(1, defValue.length() - 1);
1019 |             if (maybeStringVal.indexOf(defValue.charAt(0)) == -1) {
1020 |               options.setDefineToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1021 |               continue;
1022 |             }
1023 |           } else {
1024 |             try {
1025 |               options.setDefineToDoubleLiteral(defName,
1026 |                   Double.parseDouble(defValue));
1027 |               continue;
1028 |             } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
1029 |               // do nothing, it will be caught at the end
1030 |             }
1031 |           }
1032 |         }
1033 |       }
1034 | 
1035 |       throw new RuntimeException(
1036 |           "--define flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1037 |     }
1038 |   }

1004 |   static String identifierEscape(String s) {

265 |       // The right of the definition has side effect:
266 |       // Example, for x:
267 |       // x = readProp(b), modifyProp(b); print(x);
268 |       if (checkRightOf(def, defCfgNode, SIDE_EFFECT_PREDICATE)) {
269 |         return false;
270 |       }
271 | 
272 |       // Similar check as the above but this time, all the sub-expressions
273 |       // left of the use of the variable.
274 |       // x = readProp(b); modifyProp(b), print(x);
275 |       if (checkLeftOf(use, useCfgNode, SIDE_EFFECT_PREDICATE)) {
276 |         return false;
277 |       }
278 | 
279 |       // Similar side effect check as above but this time the side effect is
280 |       // else where along the path.
281 |       // x = readProp(b); while(modifyProp(b)) {}; print(x);
282 |       CheckPathsBetweenNodes<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>
283 |         pathCheck = new CheckPathsBetweenNodes<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>(
284 |                cfg,
285 |                cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(defCfgNode),
286 |                cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(useCfgNode),
287 |                SIDE_EFFECT_PREDICATE,
288 |                Predicates.
289 |                    <DiGraphEdge<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>>alwaysTrue(),
290 |                false);
291 |       if (pathCheck.somePathsSatisfyPredicate()) {
292 |         return false;
293 |       }
294 | 
295 |       // TODO(user): Side-effect is ok sometimes. As long as there are no
296 |       // side-effect function down all paths to the use. Once we have all the
297 |       // side-effect analysis tool.
298 |       if (NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(def.getLastChild())) {
299 |         return false;
300 |       }
301 | 
302 |       // TODO(user): We could inline all the uses if the expression is short.
303 | 
304 |       // Finally we have to make sure that there are no more than one use
305 |       // in the program and in the CFG node. Even when it is semantically
306 |       // correctly inlining twice increases code size.
307 |       if (numUseWithinUseCfgNode != 1) {
308 |         return false;
309 |       }
310 | 
311 |       // Make sure that the name is not within a loop
312 |       if (NodeUtil.isWithinLoop(use)) {
313 |         return false;
314 |       }
315 | 
316 |       // We give up inling stuff with R-Value that has GETPROP, GETELEM,
317 |       // or anything that creates a new object.
318 |       // Example:
319 |       // var x = a.b.c; j.c = 1; print(x);
320 |       // Inlining print(a.b.c) is not safe consider j and be alias to a.b.
321 |       // TODO(user): We could get more accuracy by looking more in-detail
322 |       // what j is and what x is trying to into to.
323 |       if (NodeUtil.has(def.getLastChild(),
324 |           new Predicate<Node>() {
325 |               @Override
326 |               public boolean apply(Node input) {
327 |                 switch (input.getType()) {
328 |                   case Token.GETELEM:
329 |                   case Token.GETPROP:
330 |                   case Token.ARRAYLIT:
331 |                   case Token.OBJECTLIT:
332 |                   case Token.REGEXP:
333 |                   case Token.NEW:
334 |                     return true;
335 |                 }
336 |                 return false;
337 |               }
338 |           },
339 |           new Predicate<Node>() {
340 |               @Override
341 |               public boolean apply(Node input) {
342 |                 // Recurse if the node is not a function.
343 |                 return !NodeUtil.isFunction(input);
344 |               }
345 |           })) {
346 |         return false;
347 |       }
348 | 
349 |       Collection<Node> uses = reachingUses.getUses(varName, defCfgNode);
350 | 
351 |       if (uses.size() != 1) {
352 |         return false;
353 |       }
354 | 
355 |       return true;
356 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal,Node,Node,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 680-718
Documentation:
/**
     * Updates our respresentation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
680 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
681 |         String name) {
682 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
683 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
684 |       // assignments.
685 | 
686 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
687 |       String prefix;
688 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
689 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
690 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
691 |       } else {
692 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
693 |         if (i == -1) {
694 |           return false;
695 |         }
696 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
697 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
698 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
699 |         while (i >= 0) {
700 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
701 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
702 |         }
703 |       }
704 | 
705 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
706 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
707 |         // key, so we're done.
708 |         return true;
709 |       }
710 | 
711 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
712 |         parent = n;
713 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
714 |       }
715 | 
716 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
717 |       return true;
718 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.tryRemoveAssignment(NodeTraversal,Node,Node,FlowState<LiveVariableLattice>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DeadAssignmentsElimination.java
Original range: 169-273
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if any local variables are dead after the instruction {@code n}
   * and are assigned within the subtree of {@code n}. Removes those assignments
   * if there are any.
   *
   * @param n Target instruction.
   * @param exprRoot The CFG node where the liveness information in state is
   *     still correct.
   * @param state The liveness information at {@code n}.
   */
Method code:
169 |   private void tryRemoveAssignment(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node exprRoot,
170 |       FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state) {
171 | 
172 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
173 | 
174 |     if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) ||
175 |         n.getType() == Token.INC || n.getType() == Token.DEC) {
176 | 
177 |       Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
178 |       Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
179 | 
180 |       // Recurse first. Example: dead_x = dead_y = 1; We try to clean up dead_y
181 |       // first.
182 |       if (rhs != null) {
183 |         tryRemoveAssignment(t, rhs, exprRoot, state);
184 |         rhs = lhs.getNext();
185 |       }
186 | 
187 |       Scope scope = t.getScope();
188 |       if (!NodeUtil.isName(lhs)) {
189 |         return; // Not a local variable assignment.
190 |       }
191 |       String name = lhs.getString();
192 |       if (!scope.isDeclared(name, false)) {
193 |         return;
194 |       }
195 |       Var var = scope.getVar(name);
196 | 
197 |       if (liveness.getEscapedLocals().contains(var)) {
198 |         return; // Local variable that might be escaped due to closures.
199 |       }
200 | 
201 |       // If we have an identity assignment such as a=a, always remove it
202 |       // regardless of what the liveness results because it
203 |       // does not change the result afterward.
204 |       if (rhs != null &&
205 |           NodeUtil.isName(rhs) &&
206 |           rhs.getString().equals(var.name) &&
207 |           NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
208 |         n.removeChild(rhs);
209 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, rhs);
210 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
211 |         return;
212 |       }
213 | 
214 |       if (state.getOut().isLive(var)) {
215 |         return; // Variable not dead.
216 |       }
217 | 
218 |       if (state.getIn().isLive(var) &&
219 |           isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(n, exprRoot, var.name)) {
220 |         // The variable is killed here but it is also live before it.
221 |         // This is possible if we have say:
222 |         //    if (X = a && a = C) {..} ; .......; a = S;
223 |         // In this case we are safe to remove "a = C" because it is dead.
224 |         // However if we have:
225 |         //    if (a = C && X = a) {..} ; .......; a = S;
226 |         // removing "a = C" is NOT correct, although the live set at the node
227 |         // is exactly the same.
228 |         // TODO(user): We need more fine grain CFA or we need to keep track
229 |         // of GEN sets when we recurse here.
230 |         return;
231 |       }
232 | 
233 |       if (NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
234 |         n.removeChild(rhs);
235 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, rhs);
236 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
237 |         n.removeChild(rhs);
238 |         n.removeChild(lhs);
239 |         Node op = new Node(NodeUtil.getOpFromAssignmentOp(n), lhs, rhs);
240 |         parent.replaceChild(n, op);
241 |       } else if (n.getType() == Token.INC || n.getType() == Token.DEC) {
242 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(parent)) {
243 |           parent.replaceChild(n,
244 |               new Node(Token.VOID, Node.newNumber(0).copyInformationFrom(n)));
245 |         } else if(n.getType() == Token.COMMA && n != parent.getLastChild()) {
246 |           parent.removeChild(n);
247 |         } else if (parent.getType() == Token.FOR && !NodeUtil.isForIn(parent) &&
248 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n) {
249 |           parent.replaceChild(n, new Node(Token.EMPTY));
250 |         } else {
251 |           // Cannot replace x = a++ with x = a because that's not valid
252 |           // when a is not a number.
253 |           return;
254 |         }
255 |       } else {
256 |         // Not reachable.
257 |         Preconditions.checkState(false, "Unknown statement");
258 |       }
259 | 
260 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
261 |       return;
262 | 
263 |     } else {
264 |       for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null;) {
265 |         Node next = c.getNext();
266 |         if (!ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(c)) {
267 |           tryRemoveAssignment(t, c, exprRoot, state);
268 |         }
269 |         c = next;
270 |       }
271 |       return;
272 |     }
273 |   }

/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
95 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
96 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
97 |     // just bail out early here.
98 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
99 |       return this;
100 |     }
101 | 
102 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
103 | 
104 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
105 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
106 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
107 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
108 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
109 |     }
110 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
111 |       if (alternate instanceof UnionType) {
112 |         UnionType union = (UnionType) alternate;
113 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
114 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
115 |         }
116 |       } else {
117 |         if (alternates.size() > MAX_UNION_SIZE) {
118 |           return this;
119 |         }
120 |

122 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
123 |         // one another.
124 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
125 |         while (it.hasNext()) {

127 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
128 |               current.isUnknownType()) {
129 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
130 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
131 |               return this;
132 |             }
133 |           } else {
134 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
135 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
136 |               return this;
137 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
138 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
139 |               it.remove();
140 |             }
141 |           }
142 |         }
143 |         alternates.add(alternate);
144 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
145 |       }
146 |     } else {
147 |       result = null;
148 |     }
149 |     return this;
150 |   }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 548-578
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in javascript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */

549 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {

551 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {

   * Try to fold array-length. e.g [1, 2, 3].length ==> 3, [x, y].length ==> 2
   */
Method code:
1421 |   private Node tryFoldGetProp(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
1422 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.getType() == Token.GETPROP);
1423 | 
1424 |     if (right.getType() == Token.STRING &&
1425 |         right.getString().equals("length")) {

1432 |           }

1434 |           break;

1440 |           return n;
1441 |       }

1444 |       Node lengthNode = Node.newNumber(knownLength);
1445 |       n.getParent().replaceChild(n, lengthNode);
1446 |       reportCodeChange();
1447 |

1449 |     }
1450 |
