355 |       passes.add(tightenTypesBuilder);
356 |     }
357 | 
358 |     // Property disambiguation should only run once and needs to be done
359 |     // soon after type checking, both so that it can make use of type
360 |     // information and so that other passes can take advantage of the renamed
361 |     // properties.
362 |     if (options.disambiguateProperties) {
363 |       passes.add(disambiguateProperties);
364 |     }
365 | 
366 |     if (options.computeFunctionSideEffects) {
367 |       passes.add(markPureFunctions);
368 |     } else if (options.markNoSideEffectCalls) {
369 |       // TODO(user) The properties that this pass adds to CALL and NEW
370 |       // AST nodes increase the AST's in-memory size.  Given that we are
371 |       // already running close to our memory limits, we could run into
372 |       // trouble if we end up using the @nosideeffects annotation a lot
373 |       // or compute @nosideeffects annotations by looking at function
374 |       // bodies.  It should be easy to propagate @nosideeffects
375 |       // annotations as part of passes that depend on this property and
376 |       // store the result outside the AST (which would allow garbage
377 |       // collection once the pass is done).
378 |       passes.add(markNoSideEffectCalls);
379 |     }
380 | 
381 |     if (options.chainCalls) {
382 |       passes.add(chainCalls);
383 |     }
384 | 
385 |     // Constant checking must be done after property collapsing because
386 |     // property collapsing can introduce new constants (e.g. enum values).
387 |     if (options.inlineConstantVars) {
388 |       passes.add(checkConsts);
389 |     }
390 | 
391 |     // The Caja library adds properties to Object.prototype, which breaks
392 |     // most for-in loops.  This adds a check to each loop that skips
393 |     // any property matching /___$/.
394 |     if (options.ignoreCajaProperties) {
395 |       passes.add(ignoreCajaProperties);
396 |     }
397 | 
398 |     assertAllOneTimePasses(passes);
399 | 
400 |     if (options.smartNameRemoval || options.reportPath != null) {
401 |       passes.addAll(getCodeRemovingPasses());
402 |       passes.add(smartNamePass);
403 |     }
404 | 
405 |     // TODO(user): This forces a first crack at crossModuleCodeMotion
406 |     // before devirtualization. Once certain functions are devirtualized,
407 |     // it confuses crossModuleCodeMotion ability to recognized that
408 |     // it is recursive.
409 | 
410 |     // TODO(user): This is meant for a temporary quick win.
411 |     // In the future, we might want to improve our analysis in
412 |     // CrossModuleCodeMotion so we don't need to do this.
413 |     if (options.crossModuleCodeMotion) {
414 |       passes.add(crossModuleCodeMotion);
415 |     }
416 | 
417 |     // Method devirtualization benefits from property disambiguiation so
418 |     // it should run after that pass but before passes that do
419 |     // optimizations based on global names (like cross module code motion
420 |     // and inline functions).  Smart Name Removal does better if run before
421 |     // this pass.
422 |     if (options.devirtualizePrototypeMethods) {
423 |       passes.add(devirtualizePrototypeMethods);
424 |     }
425 | 
426 |     // Running "optimizeCalls" after devirtualization is useful for removing
427 |     // unneeded "this" values.
428 |     if (options.optimizeCalls
429 |         || options.optimizeParameters
430 |         || options.optimizeReturns) {
431 |       passes.add(optimizeCalls);
432 |     }
433 | 
434 |     if (options.customPasses != null) {
435 |       passes.add(getCustomPasses(
436 |           CustomPassExecutionTime.BEFORE_OPTIMIZATION_LOOP));
437 |     }
438 | 
439 |     passes.add(createEmptyPass("beforeMainOptimizations"));
440 | 
441 |     if (options.specializeInitialModule) {
442 |       // When specializing the initial module, we want our fixups to be
443 |       // as lean as possible, so we run the entire optimization loop to a
444 |       // fixed point before specializing, then specialize, and then run the
445 |       // main optimization loop again.
446 | 
447 |       passes.addAll(getMainOptimizationLoop());
448 | 
449 |       if (options.crossModuleCodeMotion) {
450 |         passes.add(crossModuleCodeMotion);
451 |       }
452 | 
453 |       if (options.crossModuleMethodMotion) {
454 |         passes.add(crossModuleMethodMotion);
455 |       }
456 | 
457 |       passes.add(specializeInitialModule.makeOneTimePass());
458 |     }
459 | 
460 |     passes.addAll(getMainOptimizationLoop());
461 | 
462 |     passes.add(createEmptyPass("beforeModuleMotion"));
463 | 
464 |     if (options.crossModuleCodeMotion) {
465 |       passes.add(crossModuleCodeMotion);
466 |     }
467 | 
468 |     if (options.crossModuleMethodMotion) {
469 |       passes.add(crossModuleMethodMotion);
470 |     }
471 | 
472 |     passes.add(createEmptyPass("afterModuleMotion"));
473 | 
474 |     // Some optimizations belong outside the loop because running them more
475 |     // than once would either have no benefit or be incorrect.
476 |     if (options.customPasses != null) {
477 |       passes.add(getCustomPasses(
478 |           CustomPassExecutionTime.AFTER_OPTIMIZATION_LOOP));
479 |     }
480 | 
481 |     if (options.flowSensitiveInlineVariables) {
482 |       passes.add(flowSensitiveInlineVariables);
483 | 
484 |       // After inlining some of the variable uses, some variables are unused.
485 |       // Re-run remove unused vars to clean it up.
486 |       if (options.removeUnusedVars) {
487 |         passes.add(removeUnusedVars);
488 |       }
489 |     }
490 | 
491 |     if (options.collapseAnonymousFunctions) {
492 |       passes.add(collapseAnonymousFunctions);
493 |     }
494 | 
495 |     // Move functions before extracting prototype member declarations.
496 |     if (options.moveFunctionDeclarations) {
497 |       passes.add(moveFunctionDeclarations);
498 |     }
499 | 
500 |     if (options.anonymousFunctionNaming ==
501 |         AnonymousFunctionNamingPolicy.MAPPED) {
502 |       passes.add(nameMappedAnonymousFunctions);
503 |     }
504 | 
505 |     // The mapped name anonymous function pass makes use of information that
506 |     // the extract prototype member declarations pass removes so the former
507 |     // happens before the latter.
508 |     //
509 |     // Extracting prototype properties screws up the heuristic renaming
510 |     // policies, so never run it when those policies are requested.
511 |     if (options.extractPrototypeMemberDeclarations &&
512 |         (options.propertyRenaming != PropertyRenamingPolicy.HEURISTIC &&
513 |          options.propertyRenaming !=
514 |             PropertyRenamingPolicy.AGGRESSIVE_HEURISTIC)) {
515 |       passes.add(extractPrototypeMemberDeclarations);
516 |     }
517 | 
518 |     if (options.ambiguateProperties &&
519 |         (options.propertyRenaming == PropertyRenamingPolicy.ALL_UNQUOTED)) {
520 |       passes.add(ambiguateProperties);
521 |     }
522 | 
523 |     if (options.propertyRenaming != PropertyRenamingPolicy.OFF) {
524 |       passes.add(renameProperties);
525 |     }
526 | 
527 |     // Reserve global names added to the "windows" object.
528 |     if (options.reserveRawExports) {
529 |       passes.add(gatherRawExports);
530 |     }
531 | 
532 |     // This comes after property renaming because quoted property names must
533 |     // not be renamed.
534 |     if (options.convertToDottedProperties) {
535 |       passes.add(convertToDottedProperties);
536 |     }
537 | 
538 |     // Property renaming must happen before this pass runs since this
539 |     // pass may convert dotted properties into quoted properties.  It
540 |     // is beneficial to run before alias strings, alias keywords and
541 |     // variable renaming.
542 |     if (options.rewriteFunctionExpressions) {
543 |       passes.add(rewriteFunctionExpressions);
544 |     }
545 | 
546 |     // This comes after converting quoted property accesses to dotted property
547 |     // accesses in order to avoid aliasing property names.
548 |     if (!options.aliasableStrings.isEmpty() || options.aliasAllStrings) {
549 |       passes.add(aliasStrings);
550 |     }
551 | 
552 |     if (options.aliasExternals) {
553 |       passes.add(aliasExternals);
554 |     }
555 | 
556 |     if (options.aliasKeywords) {
557 |       passes.add(aliasKeywords);
558 |     }
559 | 
560 |     // Passes after this point can no longer depend on normalized AST
561 |     // assumptions.
562 |     passes.add(markUnnormalized);
563 | 
564 |     if (options.coalesceVariableNames) {
565 |       passes.add(coalesceVariableNames);
566 |     }
567 | 
568 |     if (options.collapseVariableDeclarations) {
569 |       passes.add(collapseVariableDeclarations);
570 |     }
571 | 
572 |     // This pass works best after collapseVariableDeclarations.
573 |     passes.add(denormalize);
574 | 
575 |     if (options.instrumentationTemplate != null) {
576 |       passes.add(instrumentFunctions);
577 |     }
578 | 
579 |     if (options.variableRenaming != VariableRenamingPolicy.ALL) {
580 |       // If we're leaving some (or all) variables with their old names,
581 |       // then we need to undo any of the markers we added for distinguishing
582 |       // local variables ("$$1").
583 |       passes.add(invertContextualRenaming);
584 |     }
585 | 
586 |     if (options.variableRenaming != VariableRenamingPolicy.OFF) {
587 |       passes.add(renameVars);
588 |     }
589 | 
590 |     if (options.groupVariableDeclarations) {
591 |       passes.add(groupVariableDeclarations);
592 |     }
593 | 
594 |     // This pass should run after names stop changing.
595 |     if (options.processObjectPropertyString) {
596 |       passes.add(objectPropertyStringPostprocess);
597 |     }
598 | 
599 |     if (options.labelRenaming) {
600 |       passes.add(renameLabels);
601 |     }
602 | 
603 |     if (options.anonymousFunctionNaming ==
604 |         AnonymousFunctionNamingPolicy.UNMAPPED) {
605 |       passes.add(nameUnmappedAnonymousFunctions);
606 |     }
607 | 
608 |     // Safety check
609 |     if (options.checkSymbols) {
610 |       passes.add(sanityCheckVars);
611 |     }
612 | 
613 |     return passes;
614 |   }

/**
   * Writes out js code from a root node. If printing input delimiters, this
   * method will attach a comment to the start of the text indicating which
   * input the output derived from. If there were any preserve annotations
   * within the root's source, they will also be printed in a block comment
   * at the beginning of the output.
   */
Method code:
1370 |   public void toSource(final CodeBuilder cb,
1371 |                        final int inputSeqNum,
1372 |                        final Node root) {
1373 |     runInCompilerThread(new Callable<Void>() {

1375 |         if (options.printInputDelimiter) {
1376 |           if ((cb.getLength() > 0) && !cb.endsWith("\n")) {
1377 |             cb.append("\n");  // Make sure that the label starts on a new line
1378 |           }
1379 |           Preconditions.checkState(root.getType() == Token.SCRIPT);
1380 |

1388 |             .replaceAll("%num%", String.valueOf(inputSeqNum));

1398 |         }

1401 |         // root node's mappings are offset by the given string builder buffer.
1402 |         if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null) {
1403 |           sourceMap.setStartingPosition(

1405 |         }
1406 |

1408 |         if (!code.isEmpty()) {
1409 |           cb.append(code);
1410 |           if (!code.endsWith(";")) {

494 |         next = c.getNext();
495 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
496 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
497 |         switch (c.getType()) {
498 |           case Token.LABEL:
499 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
500 |             break;
501 |           case Token.FOR:
502 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
503 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
504 |               if (first.getType() == Token.VAR) {
505 |                 // Transform:
506 |                 //    for (var a in b) {}
507 |                 // to:
508 |                 //    var a; for (a in b) {};
509 |                 Node newStatement = first.cloneTree();
510 |                 Node name = first.removeFirstChild();
511 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
512 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
513 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
514 |               }
515 |             } else if (c.getFirstChild().getType() != Token.EMPTY) {
516 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
517 |               Node empty = new Node(Token.EMPTY);
518 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
519 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
520 | 
521 |               Node newStatement;
522 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
523 |               // but are handled differently.
524 |               if (init.getType() == Token.VAR) {
525 |                 newStatement = init;
526 |               } else {
527 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
528 |               }
529 | 
530 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
531 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
532 |             }
533 |             break;
534 |         }
535 |       }
536 |     }

===== M0480 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 150-195
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
150 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
151 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
152 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
153 |       case Token.BLOCK:
154 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
155 |       case Token.TRY:
156 |       case Token.FINALLY:
157 |         return true;
158 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
159 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
160 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
161 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
162 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
163 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
164 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
165 |         // child.
166 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
167 |       case Token.WHILE:
168 |       case Token.DO:
169 |       case Token.IF:
170 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
171 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
172 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FOR:
175 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
176 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
177 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
178 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
179 |         // That way the following:
180 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
181 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
183 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
184 |         } else {
185 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
186 |         }
187 |       case Token.SWITCH:
188 |       case Token.CASE:
189 |       case Token.CATCH:
190 |       case Token.WITH:
191 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
192 |       default:
193 |         return false;
194 |     }
195 |   }

288 |         replaceMessages : createEmptyPass("replaceMessages"));

306 |     }
307 | 
308 |     assertAllOneTimePasses(checks);
309 |     return checks;
310 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldBinaryOperator(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java
Original range: 89-155
Documentation:

Method code:
89 |   private Node tryFoldBinaryOperator(Node subtree) {
90 |     Node left = subtree.getFirstChild();
91 | 
92 |     if (left == null) {
93 |       return subtree;
94 |     }
95 | 
96 |     Node right = left.getNext();
97 | 
98 |     if (right == null) {
99 |       return subtree;
100 |     }
101 | 
102 |     // If we've reached here, node is truly a binary operator.
103 |     switch(subtree.getType()) {
104 |       case Token.GETPROP:
105 |         return tryFoldGetProp(subtree, left, right);
106 | 
107 |       case Token.GETELEM:
108 |         return tryFoldGetElem(subtree, left, right);
109 | 
110 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
111 |         return tryFoldInstanceof(subtree, left, right);
112 | 
113 |       case Token.AND:
114 |       case Token.OR:
115 |         return tryFoldAndOr(subtree, left, right);
116 | 
117 |       case Token.LSH:
118 |       case Token.RSH:
119 |       case Token.URSH:
120 |         return tryFoldShift(subtree, left, right);
121 | 
122 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
123 |         return tryFoldAssign(subtree, left, right);
124 | 
125 |       case Token.ADD:
126 |         return tryFoldAdd(subtree, left, right);
127 | 
128 |       case Token.SUB:
129 |       case Token.DIV:
130 |       case Token.MOD:
131 |         return tryFoldArithmeticOp(subtree, left, right);
132 | 
133 |       case Token.MUL:
134 |       case Token.BITAND:
135 |       case Token.BITOR:
136 |         Node result = tryFoldArithmeticOp(subtree, left, right);
137 |         if (result != subtree) {
138 |           return result;
139 |         }
140 |         return tryFoldLeftChildOp(subtree, left, right);
141 | 
142 |       case Token.LT:
143 |       case Token.GT:
144 |       case Token.LE:
145 |       case Token.GE:
146 |       case Token.EQ:
147 |       case Token.NE:
148 |       case Token.SHEQ:
149 |       case Token.SHNE:
150 |         return tryFoldComparison(subtree, left, right);
151 | 
152 |       default:
153 |         return subtree;
154 |     }
155 |   }

===== M0516 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 416-438
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An rvalue in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
416 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
417 |       switch (n.getType()) {
418 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
419 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
420 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
421 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
422 |         case Token.OR:
423 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
424 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
425 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
426 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
427 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
428 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
429 |         case Token.HOOK:
430 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
431 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
432 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
433 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
434 |           Node third = second.getNext();
435 |           return getValueType(third);
436 |       }
437 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
438 |     }

204 |   private Node transform(AstNode node) {
205 |     JSDocInfo jsDocInfo = handleJsDoc(node);

207 |     if (jsDocInfo != null) {
208 |       irNode.setJSDocInfo(jsDocInfo);

72 |     // Global scope _SHOULD_ work, however, liveness won't finish without
73 |     // -Xmx1024 in closure. We might have to look at coding conventions for

===== M0606 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.removeUnreferencedVars()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 711-770
Documentation:
/**
   * Removes any vars in the scope that were not referenced. Removes any
   * assigments to those variables as well.
   */
Method code:
711 |   private void removeUnreferencedVars() {
712 |     CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
713 | 
714 |     for (Iterator<Var> it = maybeUnreferenced.iterator(); it.hasNext(); ) {
715 |       Var var = it.next();
716 | 
717 |       // Regardless of what happens to the original declaration,
718 |       // we need to remove all assigns, because they may contain references
719 |       // to other unreferenced variables.
720 |       removeAllAssigns(var);
721 | 
722 |       compiler.addToDebugLog("Unreferenced var: " + var.name);
723 |       Node nameNode = var.nameNode;
724 |       Node toRemove = nameNode.getParent();
725 |       Node parent = toRemove.getParent();
726 | 
727 |       Preconditions.checkState(
728 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR ||
729 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.FUNCTION ||
730 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.LP &&
731 |           parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION,
732 |           "We should only declare vars and functions and function args");
733 | 
734 |       if (toRemove.getType() == Token.LP &&
735 |           parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
736 |         // Don't remove function arguments here. That's a special case
737 |         // that's taken care of in removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs.
738 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(toRemove)) {
739 |         if (!preserveFunctionExpressionNames) {
740 |           toRemove.getFirstChild().setString("");
741 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
742 |         }
743 |         // Don't remove bleeding functions.
744 |       } else if (parent != null &&
745 |           parent.getType() == Token.FOR &&
746 |           parent.getChildCount() < 4) {
747 |         // foreach iterations have 3 children. Leave them alone.
748 |       } else if (toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR &&
749 |           nameNode.hasChildren() &&
750 |           NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
751 |         // If this is a single var declaration, we can at least remove the

757 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
758 |         }
759 |       } else if (toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR &&
760 |           toRemove.getChildCount() > 1) {
761 |         // For var declarations with multiple names (i.e. var a, b, c),
762 |         // only remove the unreferenced name

764 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();

769 |     }

421 |     private boolean isInlineableDeclaredConstant(Var var,

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/FunctionType.java
Original range: 751-793
Documentation:
/**
   * A function is a subtype of another if their call methods are related via
   * subtyping and {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that} with regard to
   * the prototype chain.
   */
Method code:
751 |   @Override
752 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
753 |     if (JSType.isSubtype(this, that)) {
754 |       return true;
755 |     }
756 | 
757 |     if (that.isFunctionType()) {
758 |       if (((FunctionType) that).isInterface()) {
759 |         // Any function can be assigned to an interface function.
760 |         return true;
761 |       }
762 |       if (this.isInterface()) {
763 |         // An interface function cannot be assigned to anything.
764 |         return false;
765 |       }
766 |       // If functionA is a subtype of functionB, then their "this" types
767 |       // should be contravariant. However, this causes problems because
768 |       // of the way we enforce overrides. Because function(this:SubFoo)
769 |       // is not a subtype of function(this:Foo), our override check treats
770 |       // this as an error. It also screws up out standard method
771 |       // for aliasing constructors. Let's punt on all this for now.
772 |       // TODO(nicksantos): fix this.
773 |       FunctionType other = (FunctionType) that;
774 |       boolean treatThisTypesAsCovariant =
775 |         // If either one of these is a ctor, skip 'this' checking.
776 |         this.isConstructor() || other.isConstructor() ||
777 | 
778 |         // An interface 'this'-type is non-restrictive.
779 |         // In practical terms, if C implements I, and I has a method m,
780 |         // then any m doesn't necessarily have to C#m's 'this'
781 |         // type doesn't need to match I.
782 |         (other.typeOfThis.getConstructor() != null &&
783 |              other.typeOfThis.getConstructor().isInterface()) ||
784 | 
785 |         // If one of the 'this' types is covariant of the other,
786 |         // then we'll treat them as covariant (see comment above).
787 |         other.typeOfThis.isSubtype(this.typeOfThis) ||
788 |         this.typeOfThis.isSubtype(other.typeOfThis);
789 |       return treatThisTypesAsCovariant && this.call.isSubtype(other.call);
790 |     }
791 | 
792 |     return getNativeType(JSTypeNative.FUNCTION_PROTOTYPE).isSubtype(that);
793 |   }

===== M0631 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 635-680
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assigments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
635 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
636 |     boolean changes = false;
637 |     do {
638 |       changes = false;
639 | 
640 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
641 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
642 |       // we traverse it.
643 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
644 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
645 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
646 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
647 |           current--;
648 |         } else {
649 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
650 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
651 | 
652 |           if (var.getParentNode().getType() == Token.VAR &&
653 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
654 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
655 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
656 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
657 |           } else {
658 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
659 |             // or a for...in variable.
660 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
661 |           }
662 | 
663 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
664 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
665 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
666 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
667 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
668 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
669 |             }
670 |           }
671 | 
672 |           if (assignedToUnknownValue && hasPropertyAssign) {
673 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
674 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
675 |             current--;
676 |           }
677 |         }
678 |       }
679 |     } while (changes);
680 |   }

Documentation:
/**
   * Given an entry node, find all the nodes reachable from that node
   * and prioritize them.
   */
Method code:
196 |   private void prioritizeFromEntryNode(DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry) {
197 |     PriorityQueue<DiGraphNode<Node, Branch>> worklist =
198 |         new PriorityQueue<DiGraphNode<Node, Branch>>(10, priorityComparator);
199 |     worklist.add(entry);
200 | 
201 |     while (!worklist.isEmpty()) {
202 |       DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> current = worklist.remove();
203 |       if (nodePriorities.containsKey(current)) {
204 |         continue;
205 |       }
206 | 
207 |       nodePriorities.put(current, ++priorityCounter);
208 | 
209 |       List<DiGraphNode<Node, Branch>> successors =
210 |           cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(current);
211 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : successors) {
212 |         worklist.add(candidate);
213 |       }
214 |     }
215 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal.traverseRoots(List<Node>)

Original range: 260-282
Documentation:

Method code:
260 |   public void traverseRoots(List<Node> roots) {
261 |     if (roots.isEmpty()) {
262 |       return;
263 |     }
264 | 
265 |     try {
266 |       Node scopeRoot = roots.get(0).getParent();
267 |       Preconditions.checkState(scopeRoot != null);
268 | 
269 |       sourceName = "";
270 |       curNode = scopeRoot;
271 |       pushScope(scopeRoot);
272 | 
273 |       for (Node root : roots) {
274 |         Preconditions.checkState(root.getParent() == scopeRoot);
275 |         traverseBranch(root, scopeRoot);
276 |       }
277 | 
278 |       popScope();
279 |     } catch (Exception unexpectedException) {
280 |       throwUnexpectedException(unexpectedException);
281 |     }
282 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 117-170
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
117 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
118 |     switch (n.getType()) {
119 |       case Token.VAR:
120 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
121 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
122 |              child != null;) {
123 |           Node next = child.getNext();
124 |           declareVar(child);
125 |           child = next;
126 |         }
127 |         return;
128 | 
129 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
130 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
131 |           return;
132 |         }
133 | 
134 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
135 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
136 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
137 |           return;
138 |         }
139 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
140 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
141 | 
142 |       case Token.CATCH:
143 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
144 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME);
145 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
146 |         // is the code block
147 | 
148 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
149 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
150 | 
151 |         declareVar(var);
152 |         scanVars(block, n);
153 |         return;  // only one child to scan
154 | 
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |         sourceName = (String) n.getProp(Node.SOURCENAME_PROP);
157 |         break;
158 |     }
159 | 
160 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
161 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
162 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
163 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
164 |            child != null;) {
165 |         Node next = child.getNext();
166 |         scanVars(child, n);
167 |         child = next;
168 |       }
169 |     }
170 |   }

408 |   @Override
409 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
410 |     if (JSType.isSubtype(this, that)) {
411 |       return true;
412 |     }
413 | 
414 |     // Union types
415 |     if (that instanceof UnionType) {
416 |       // The static {@code JSType.isSubtype} check already decomposed
417 |       // union types, so we don't need to check those again.
418 |       return false;
419 |     }
420 | 
421 |     // record types
422 |     if (that instanceof RecordType) {
423 |       return RecordType.isSubtype(this, (RecordType) that);
424 |     }
425 | 
426 |     // Interfaces
427 |     // Find all the interfaces implemented by this class and compare each one
428 |     // to the interface instance.
429 |     ObjectType thatObj = that.toObjectType();
430 |     ObjectType thatCtor = thatObj == null ? null : thatObj.getConstructor();
431 |     if (thatCtor != null && thatCtor.isInterface()) {
432 |       Iterable<ObjectType> thisInterfaces = getCtorImplementedInterfaces();
433 |       for (ObjectType thisInterface : thisInterfaces) {
434 |         if (thisInterface.isSubtype(that)) {
435 |           return true;
436 |         }
437 |       }
438 |     }
439 | 
440 |     // other prototype based objects
441 |     if (that != null) {
442 |       if (isUnknownType() || implicitPrototypeChainIsUnknown()) {
443 |         // If unsure, say 'yes', to avoid spurious warnings.
444 |         // TODO(user): resolve the prototype chain completely in all cases,
445 |         // to avoid guessing.
446 |         return true;
447 |       }
448 |       return this.isImplicitPrototype(thatObj);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(Set<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 404-476
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
404 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
405 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
406 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
407 | 
408 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
409 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator = prefix.isEmpty() ?
410 |         globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(reservedNames, "",
411 |         reservedCharacters);
412 | 
413 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
414 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
415 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
416 | 
417 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
418 |       if (a.newName != null) {
419 |         continue;
420 |       }
421 | 
422 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
423 |         continue;
424 |       }
425 | 
426 |       String newName;
427 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
428 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
429 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
430 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
431 |       } else {
432 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
433 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
434 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
435 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
436 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
437 |       }
438 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
439 |     }
440 | 
441 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
442 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
443 |     // follows:
444 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
445 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
446 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
447 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
448 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
449 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
450 |     //    compressible.
451 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
452 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
453 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
454 | 
455 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
456 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
457 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
458 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
459 | 
460 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
461 |       // generated names of the same length.
462 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
463 |       for (int j = i;
464 |            j < numPendingAssignments &&
465 |                generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len;
466 |            j++) {
467 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
468 |       }
469 | 
470 |       // Now, make the assignments
471 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
472 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
473 |         ++i;
474 |       }
475 |     }
476 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Original range: 112-199

Method code:
112 |   @Override
113 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
114 |     if (n.getType() != Token.NAME) {
115 |       return;
116 |     }
117 | 
118 |     String varName = n.getString();
119 | 
120 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
121 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
122 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunction(parent));
123 | 
124 |       // A function declaration with an empty name passes Rhino,
125 |       // but is supposed to be a syntax error according to the spec.
126 |       if (!NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
127 |         t.report(n, INVALID_FUNCTION_DECL);
128 |       }
129 |       return;
130 |     }
131 | 
132 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
133 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
134 |     if ((parent.getType() == Token.VAR ||
135 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
136 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
137 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
138 | 
139 |       parent.addSuppression("duplicate");
140 |     }
141 | 
142 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
143 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
144 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
145 |     if (var == null) {
146 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
147 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
148 |         // current scope.
149 |       } else {
150 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
151 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
152 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
153 |         }
154 | 
155 |         if (sanityCheck) {
156 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
157 |         } else {
158 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
159 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
160 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
161 |         }
162 |       }
163 |       return;
164 |     }
165 | 
166 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
167 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
168 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
169 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
170 |       return;
171 |     }
172 | 
173 |     // Check module dependencies.
174 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
175 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
176 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
177 |     if (varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
178 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
179 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
180 |       } else {
181 |         if (!sanityCheck && scope.isGlobal()) {
182 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
183 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
184 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
185 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
186 |           } else {
187 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
188 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
189 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
190 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
191 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
192 |           }
193 |         } else {
194 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |         }
197 |       }
198 |     }
199 |   }

===== M0698 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeArgumentsArray.java
Original range: 178-290
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
178 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
179 | 
180 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
181 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.getType() == Token.LP);
182 | 
183 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
184 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
185 |     boolean changed = false;
186 | 
187 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
188 |     // array.
189 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
190 | 
191 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
192 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
193 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
194 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
195 | 
196 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
197 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
198 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
199 | 
200 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
201 | 
202 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
203 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
204 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
205 |       if (getElem.getType() != Token.GETELEM) {
206 |         return false;
207 |       }
208 | 
209 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
210 | 
211 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
212 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
213 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
214 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
215 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
216 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
217 |         // it is never 'callee'.
218 |         return false; // Give up.
219 |       }
220 | 
221 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
222 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
223 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
224 |       if (NodeUtil.isCall(getElemParent) &&
225 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
226 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
227 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
228 |         return false;
229 |       }
230 | 
231 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
232 |       // than all the one we saw before.
233 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
234 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
235 |         highestIndex = value;
236 |       }
237 |     }
238 | 
239 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
240 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
241 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
242 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
243 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
244 | 
245 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
246 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
247 | 
248 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
249 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
250 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
251 |       String name = getNewName();
252 |       argNames[i] = name;
253 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(Node.newString(Token.NAME, name));
254 |       changed = true;
255 |     }
256 | 
257 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
258 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
259 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
260 | 
261 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
262 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
263 |         continue;
264 |       }
265 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
266 | 
267 |       // Unnamed parameter.
268 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
269 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
270 |             Node.newString(Token.NAME, argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
271 |       } else {
272 | 
273 |         // Here, for no apparent reason, the user is accessing a named parameter
274 |         // with arguments[idx]. We can replace it with the actual name for them.
275 |         Node name = parametersList.getFirstChild();
276 | 
277 |         // This is a linear search for the actual name from the signature.
278 |         // It is not necessary to make this fast because chances are the user
279 |         // will not deliberately write code like this.
280 |         for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) {
281 |           name = name.getNext();
282 |         }
283 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
284 |             Node.newString(Token.NAME, name.getString()));
285 |       }
286 |       changed = true;
287 |     }
288 | 
289 |     return changed;
290 |   }

483 |         // then it must have a DIRECT_EVAL annotation. If it does not, then
484 |         // that means it was originally an indirect call to eval, and that

486 |         // 2) If the left hand side of the call is a property reference,

488 |         // that means it was originally an call without an explicit this and

580 |       case Token.NEW:

585 |         // to force parentheses. Otherwise, when parsed, NEW will bind to the
586 |         // first viable parentheses (don't traverse into functions).
587 |         if (NodeUtil.containsType(first, Token.CALL, new MatchNotFunction())) {
588 |           precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType()) + 1;
589 |         }
590 |         addExpr(first, precedence);
591 | 
592 |         // '()' is optional when no arguments are present
593 |         Node next = first.getNext();
594 |         if (next != null) {
595 |           add("(");
596 |           addList(next);
597 |           add(")");
598 |         }
599 |         break;
600 | 
601 |       case Token.STRING:
602 |         if (childCount !=
603 |             ((n.getParent() != null &&
604 |               n.getParent().getType() == Token.OBJECTLIT) ? 1 : 0)) {
605 |           throw new IllegalStateException(
606 |               "Unexpected String children: " + n.getParent().toStringTree());
607 |         }
608 |         add(jsString(n.getString(), outputCharsetEncoder));
609 |         break;
610 | 
611 |       case Token.DELPROP:
612 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
613 |         add("delete ");
614 |         add(first);
615 |         break;
616 | 
617 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
618 |         boolean needsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
619 |         if (needsParens) {
620 |           add("(");
621 |         }
622 |         add("{");
623 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
624 |           if (c != first) {
625 |             cc.listSeparator();
626 |           }
627 | 
628 |           if (c.getType() == Token.GET || c.getType() == Token.SET) {
629 |             add(c);
630 |           } else {
631 |             // Object literal property names don't have to be quoted if they are
632 |             // not JavaScript keywords
633 |             if (c.getType() == Token.STRING &&
634 |                 !TokenStream.isKeyword(c.getString()) &&
635 |                 TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(c.getString()) &&
636 |                 // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that were
637 |                 // unicode escaped.
638 |                 NodeUtil.isLatin(c.getString())) {
639 |               add(c.getString());
640 |             } else {
641 |               addExpr(c, 1);
642 |             }
643 |             add(":");
644 |             addExpr(c.getFirstChild(), 1);
645 |           }
646 |         }
647 |         add("}");
648 |         if (needsParens) {
649 |           add(")");
650 |         }
651 |         break;
652 |       }
653 | 
654 |       case Token.SWITCH:
655 |         add("switch(");
656 |         add(first);
657 |         add(")");
658 |         cc.beginBlock();
659 |         addAllSiblings(first.getNext());
660 |         cc.endBlock(context == Context.STATEMENT);
661 |         break;
662 | 
663 |       case Token.CASE:
664 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
665 |         add("case ");
666 |         add(first);
667 |         addCaseBody(last);
668 |         break;
669 | 
670 |       case Token.DEFAULT:
671 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
672 |         add("default");
673 |         addCaseBody(first);
674 |         break;
675 | 
676 |       case Token.LABEL:
677 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
678 |         if (first.getType() != Token.LABEL_NAME) {
679 |           throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
680 |         }
681 |         add(first);
682 |         add(":");
683 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
684 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), true);
685 |         break;
686 | 
687 |       // This node is auto generated in anonymous functions and should just get
688 |       // ignored for our purposes.
689 |       case Token.SETNAME:
690 |         break;
691 | 
692 |       default:
693 |         throw new Error("Unknown type " + type + "\n" + n.toStringTree());
694 |     }
695 | 
696 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);
697 |   }

/**
     * If this is an assign to a variable or its property, return it.
     * Otherwise, return null.
     */
Method code:
835 |     static Assign maybeCreateAssign(Node assignNode) {
836 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(assignNode));
837 | 
838 |       // Skip one level of GETPROPs or GETELEMs.
839 |       //
840 |       // Don't skip more than one level, because then we get into

842 |       // trigger side-effects, and the variable they're on cannot be removed.

852 |           // property sets.
853 |           current = current.getFirstChild();
854 |         }
855 |       }
856 |

858 |         return new Assign(assignNode, current, isPropAssign);
859 |       }
860 |       return null;
861 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 108-141
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   */
Method code:
108 |   static TernaryValue getBooleanValue(Node n) {
109 |     switch (n.getType()) {
110 |       case Token.STRING:
111 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
112 | 
113 |       case Token.NUMBER:
114 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
115 | 
116 |       case Token.NULL:
117 |       case Token.FALSE:
118 |       case Token.VOID:
119 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
120 | 
121 |       case Token.NAME:
122 |         String name = n.getString();
123 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
124 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
125 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
126 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
127 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
128 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
129 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
130 |         }
131 |         break;
132 | 
133 |       case Token.TRUE:
134 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
135 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
136 |       case Token.REGEXP:
137 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
138 |     }
139 | 
140 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
141 |   }

148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

/**
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param cfgNode The node to add
   * @param conditional true if the definition is not always executed.
   */
Method code:
220 |   private void computeMustDef(
221 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, MustDef output, boolean conditional) {
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 | 
224 |       case Token.BLOCK:
225 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
226 |         return;
227 | 
228 |       case Token.WHILE:
229 |       case Token.DO:
230 |       case Token.IF:
231 |         computeMustDef(
232 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
233 |         return;
234 | 
235 |       case Token.FOR:
236 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
237 |           computeMustDef(
238 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
239 |         } else {
240 |           // for(x in y) {...}
241 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
242 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
243 |           if (NodeUtil.isVar(lhs)) {
244 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
245 |           }
246 |           if (NodeUtil.isName(lhs)) {
247 |             addToDefIfLocal(lhs.getString(), cfgNode, rhs, output);
248 |           }
249 |         }
250 |         return;
251 | 
252 |       case Token.AND:
253 |       case Token.OR:
254 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
255 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
256 |         return;
257 | 
258 |       case Token.HOOK:
259 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
260 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
261 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
262 |         return;
263 | 
264 |       case Token.VAR:
265 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
266 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
267 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
268 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
269 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
270 |           }
271 |         }
272 |         return;
273 | 
274 |       default:
275 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isName(n.getFirstChild())) {
276 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
277 |           computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
278 |           addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
279 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
280 |         } else {
281 | 
282 |           // DEC and INC actually defines the variable.
283 |           if (n.getType() == Token.DEC || n.getType() == Token.INC) {
284 |             Node target = n.getFirstChild();
285 |             if (NodeUtil.isName(target)) {
286 |               addToDefIfLocal(target.getString(),
287 |                   conditional ? null : cfgNode, null, output);
288 |               return;
289 |             }
290 |           }
291 | 
292 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
293 |             computeMustDef(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
294 |           }
295 |         }
296 |     }
297 |   }

570 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {

Original range: 900-975
Documentation:
/*
   *  0 comma ,
   *  1 assignment = += -= *= /= %= <<= >>= >>>= &= ^= |=
   *  2 conditional ?:
   *  3 logical-or ||
   *  4 logical-and &&
   *  5 bitwise-or |
   *  6 bitwise-xor ^
   *  7 bitwise-and &
   *  8 equality == !=
   *  9 relational < <= > >=
   * 10 bitwise shift << >> >>>
   * 11 addition/subtraction + -
   * 12 multiply/divide * / %
   * 13 negation/increment ! ~ - ++ --
   * 14 call, member () [] .
   */
Method code:
900 |   static int precedence(int type) {

Original range: 113-134
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
113 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
114 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
115 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
116 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
117 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
118 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
119 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
120 | 
121 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
122 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
123 |         }
124 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
125 |       } else {
126 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
127 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
128 |       }
129 |     }
130 | 
131 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
132 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
133 |     }
134 |   }

/**
   * Try to fold comparison nodes, e.g ==

739 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
740 |   private Node tryFoldComparison(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
741 |     if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(left, false) ||
742 |         !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(right, false)) {
743 |       // We only handle non-literal operands for LT and GT.
744 |       if (n.getType() != Token.GT && n.getType() != Token.LT) {
745 |         return n;
746 |       }
747 |     }
748 | 
749 |     int op = n.getType();
750 |     boolean result;
751 | 
752 |     // TODO(johnlenz): Use the JSType to compare nodes of different types.
753 | 
754 |     boolean rightLiteral = NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(right, false);
755 |     boolean undefinedRight = ((Token.NAME == right.getType()
756 |           && right.getString().equals("undefined"))

760 |     switch (left.getType()) {
761 |       case Token.VOID:
762 |         if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(left.getFirstChild(), false)) {
763 |           return n;
764 |         } else if (!rightLiteral) {
765 |           return n;
766 |         } else {
767 |           result = compareToUndefined(right, op);
768 |         }
769 |         break;
770 | 
771 |       case Token.NULL:
772 |       case Token.TRUE:
773 |       case Token.FALSE:
774 |         if (undefinedRight) {
775 |           result = compareToUndefined(left, op);
776 |           break;
777 |         }
778 |         int rhType = right.getType();
779 |         if (rhType != Token.TRUE &&
780 |             rhType != Token.FALSE &&
781 |             rhType != Token.NULL) {
782 |           return n;
783 |         }
784 |         switch (op) {
785 |           case Token.SHEQ:
786 |           case Token.EQ:
787 |             result = left.getType() == right.getType();
788 |             break;
789 | 
790 |           case Token.SHNE:
791 |           case Token.NE:
792 |             result = left.getType() != right.getType();
793 |             break;
794 | 
795 |           case Token.GE:
796 |           case Token.LE:
797 |           case Token.GT:
798 |           case Token.LT:
799 |             Boolean compareResult = compareAsNumbers(op, left, right);
800 |             if (compareResult != null) {
801 |               result = compareResult;
802 |             } else {
803 |               return n;
804 |             }
805 |             break;
806 | 
807 |           default:
808 |             return n;  // we only handle == and != here
809 |         }
810 |         break;
811 | 
812 |       case Token.THIS:
813 |         if (right.getType() != Token.THIS) {
814 |           return n;
815 |         }
816 |         switch (op) {
817 |           case Token.SHEQ:
818 |           case Token.EQ:
819 |             result = true;
820 |             break;
821 | 
822 |           case Token.SHNE:
823 |           case Token.NE:
824 |             result = false;
825 |             break;
826 | 
827 |           // We can only handle == and != here.
828 |           // GT, LT, GE, LE depend on the type of "this" and how it will
829 |           // be converted to number.  The results are different depending on
830 |           // whether it is a string, NaN or other number value.
831 |           default:
832 |             return n;
833 |         }
834 |         break;
835 | 
836 |       case Token.STRING:
837 |         if (undefinedRight) {
838 |           result = compareToUndefined(left, op);
839 |           break;
840 |         }
841 |         if (Token.STRING != right.getType()) {
842 |           return n;  // Only eval if they are the same type
843 |         }
844 |         switch (op) {
845 |           case Token.SHEQ:
846 |           case Token.EQ:
847 |             result = left.getString().equals(right.getString());
848 |             break;
849 | 
850 |           case Token.SHNE:
851 |           case Token.NE:
852 |             result = !left.getString().equals(right.getString());
853 |             break;
854 | 
855 |           default:
856 |             return n;  // we only handle == and != here
857 |         }
858 |         break;
859 | 
860 |       case Token.NUMBER:
861 |         if (undefinedRight) {
862 |           result = compareToUndefined(left, op);
863 |           break;
864 |         }
865 |         if (Token.NUMBER != right.getType()) {
866 |           return n;  // Only eval if they are the same type
867 |         }
868 |         Boolean compareResult = compareAsNumbers(op, left, right);
869 |         if (compareResult != null) {
870 |           result = compareResult;
871 |         } else {
872 |           return null;
873 |         }
874 |         break;
875 | 
876 |       case Token.NAME:
877 |         if (undefinedRight) {
878 |           result = compareToUndefined(left, op);
879 |           break;
880 |         }
881 | 
882 |         if (rightLiteral) {
883 |           boolean undefinedLeft = (left.getString().equals("undefined"));
884 |           if (undefinedLeft) {
885 |             result = compareToUndefined(right, op);
886 |             break;
887 |           }
888 |         }
889 | 
890 |         if (Token.NAME != right.getType()) {
891 |           return n;  // Only eval if they are the same type
892 |         }
893 |         String ln = left.getString();
894 |         String rn = right.getString();
895 |         if (!ln.equals(rn)) {
896 |           return n;  // Not the same value name.
897 |         }
898 | 
899 |         switch (op) {
900 |           // If we knew the named value wouldn't be NaN, it would be nice
901 |           // to handle EQ,NE,LE,GE,SHEQ, and SHNE.
902 |           case Token.LT:
903 |           case Token.GT:
904 |             result = false;
905 |             break;
906 |           default:
907 |             return n;  // don't handle that op
908 |         }
909 |         break;
910 | 
911 |       default:
912 |         // assert, this should cover all consts
913 |         return n;
914 |     }
915 | 
916 |     Node newNode = new Node(result ? Token.TRUE : Token.FALSE);
917 |     n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newNode);
918 |     reportCodeChange();
919 | 
920 |     return newNode;
921 |   }

/**
   * Creates a tree hierarchy representing a typed argument list.
   *
   * @param lastVarArgs whether the last type should considered as a variable
   *     length argument.
   * @param parameterTypes the parameter types. The last element of this array

1151 |   private Node createParameters(boolean lastVarArgs, JSType... parameterTypes) {
1152 |     FunctionParamBuilder builder = new FunctionParamBuilder(this);

===== M0828 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.TransformDispatcher.parseDirectives(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/IRFactory.java
Original range: 361-376
Documentation:
/**
     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *
     * For information on ES5 directives, see section 14.1 of
     * Ecma-262, Edition 5.
     *
     * It would be nice if Rhino would eventually take care of this for
     * us, but right now their directive-processing is a one-off.
     */
Method code:
361 |     private void parseDirectives(Node node) {
362 |       // Remove all the directives, and encode them in the AST.
363 |       Set<String> directives = null;
364 |       while (isDirective(node.getFirstChild())) {
365 |         String directive = node.removeFirstChild().getFirstChild().getString();
366 |         if (directives == null) {
367 |           directives = Sets.newHashSet(directive);
368 |         } else {
369 |           directives.add(directive);
370 |         }
371 |       }
372 | 
373 |       if (directives != null) {
374 |         node.setDirectives(directives);
375 |       }
376 |     }

/**
     * There are two types of calls we are interested in calls without explicit
     * "this" values (what we are call "free" calls) and direct call to eval.
     */

175 |     private void annotateCalls(Node n) {

===== M0838 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CheckSideEffects.java
Original range: 47-118
Documentation:

Method code:
47 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
48 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
49 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
50 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
51 |     // so we'll allow it.
52 |     if (n.getType() == Token.EMPTY ||
53 |         n.getType() == Token.COMMA) {
54 |       return;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     if (parent == null)
58 |       return;
59 | 
60 |     int pt = parent.getType();
61 |     if (pt == Token.COMMA) {
62 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
63 |       if (gramps.getType() == Token.CALL &&
64 |           parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
65 |         // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
66 |         // call to an eval. See Ecma-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's ok for the first
67 |         // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
68 |         // an eval.
69 |         if (n == parent.getFirstChild() &&
70 |             parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
71 |             n.getNext().getType() == Token.NAME &&
72 |             "eval".equals(n.getNext().getString())) {
73 |           return;
74 |         }
75 |       }
76 | 
77 |       if (n == parent.getLastChild()) {
78 |         for (Node an : parent.getAncestors()) {
79 |           int ancestorType = an.getType();
80 |           if (ancestorType == Token.COMMA)
81 |             continue;
82 |           if (ancestorType != Token.EXPR_RESULT &&
83 |               ancestorType != Token.BLOCK)
84 |             return;
85 |           else
86 |             break;
87 |         }
88 |       }
89 |     } else if (pt != Token.EXPR_RESULT && pt != Token.BLOCK) {
90 |       if (pt == Token.FOR && parent.getChildCount() == 4 &&
91 |           (n == parent.getFirstChild() ||
92 |            n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext())) {
93 |         // Fall through and look for warnings for the 1st and 3rd child
94 |         // of a for.
95 |       } else {
96 |         return;  // it might be ok to not have a side-effect
97 |       }
98 |     }
99 |     if (NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType()) ||
100 |         !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler())) {
101 |       if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
102 |         // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
103 |         // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
104 |         return;
105 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(n)) {
106 |         // we already reported the problem when we visited the child.
107 |         return;
108 |       }
109 | 
110 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
111 |       if (n.getType() == Token.STRING) {
112 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       t.getCompiler().report(
116 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
117 |     }
118 |   }

===== M0865 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.traverseNode(Node,Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 175-249
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
175 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
176 |     int type = n.getType();
177 |     Var var = null;
178 |     switch (type) {
179 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
180 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
181 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
183 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
184 |         }
185 | 
186 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
187 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
188 |         } else {
189 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
190 |         }
191 |         return;
192 | 
193 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
194 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
195 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
196 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
197 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
198 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
199 |           if (var != null) {
200 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
201 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
202 | 
203 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
204 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
205 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
206 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
207 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
208 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
209 |               return;
210 |             }
211 |           }
212 |         }
213 |         break;
214 | 
215 |       case Token.NAME:
216 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
217 |         if (parent.getType() == Token.VAR) {
218 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
219 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
220 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value)) {
221 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
222 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
223 |             // of traversing immediately.
224 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
225 |             return;
226 |           }
227 |         } else {
228 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
229 |           // are references to other vars.
230 |           if (var != null) {
231 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
232 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
233 |             // for now.
234 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
235 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
236 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
237 |               }
238 |             } else {
239 |               markReferencedVar(var);
240 |             }
241 |           }
242 |         }
243 |         break;
244 |     }
245 | 
246 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
247 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
248 |     }
249 |   }

/**
     * Determines whether a set operation is a constructor or enumeration
     * declaration. The set operation may either be an assignment to a name,
     * a variable declaration, or an object literal key mapping.
     *
     * @param n The node that represents the name being set
     * @param parent Parent node of {@code n} (an ASSIGN, VAR, or OBJLIT node)
     * @return Whether the set operation is either a constructor or enum
     *     declaration
     */
Method code:
483 |     private boolean isConstructorOrEnumDeclaration(Node n, Node parent) {
484 |       // NOTE(nicksantos): This does not handle named constructors
485 |       // function a() {}
486 |       // For legacy reasons, we should not fix this, because we do not
487 |       // know who's depending on the current behavior.
488 | 
489 |       JSDocInfo info;
490 |       int valueNodeType;
491 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
492 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
493 |           info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
494 |           valueNodeType = n.getNext().getType();
495 |           break;
496 |         case Token.VAR:
497 |           info = n.getJSDocInfo();
498 |           if (info == null) {
499 |             info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
500 |           }
501 |           Node valueNode = n.getFirstChild();
502 |           valueNodeType = valueNode != null ? valueNode.getType() : Token.VOID;
503 |           break;
504 |         default:
505 |           return false;
506 |       }
507 |       // Heed the annotations only if they're sensibly used.
508 |       return info != null &&
509 |              (info.isConstructor() && valueNodeType == Token.FUNCTION ||
510 |               info.hasEnumParameterType() && valueNodeType == Token.OBJECTLIT);
511 |     }
