Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(NodeTraversal,ControlFlowGraph<Node>,Set<Var>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 199-292
Documentation:

Method code:
199 |   private UndiGraph<Var, Void> computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(
200 |       NodeTraversal t, ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg, Set<Var> escaped) {
201 |     UndiGraph<Var, Void> interferenceGraph =
202 |         LinkedUndirectedGraph.create();
203 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
204 | 
205 |     // First create a node for each non-escaped variable.
206 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = scope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
207 |       Var v = i.next();
208 |       if (!escaped.contains(v)) {
209 | 
210 |         // TODO(user): In theory, we CAN coalesce function names just like
211 |         // any variables. Our Liveness analysis captures this just like it as
212 |         // described in the specification. However, we saw some zipped and
213 |         // and unzipped size increase after this. We are not totally sure why
214 |         // that is but, for now, we will respect the dead functions and not play
215 |         // around with it.
216 |         if (!NodeUtil.isFunction(v.getParentNode())) {
217 |           interferenceGraph.createNode(v);
218 |         }
219 |       }
220 |     }
221 | 
222 |     // Go through each variable and try to connect them.
223 |     for (Iterator<Var> i1 = scope.getVars(); i1.hasNext();) {
224 |       Var v1 = i1.next();
225 | 
226 |       NEXT_VAR_PAIR:
227 |       for (Iterator<Var> i2 = scope.getVars(); i2.hasNext();) {
228 |         Var v2 = i2.next();
229 | 
230 |         // Skip duplicate pairs.
231 |         if (v1.index >= v2.index) {
232 |           continue;
233 |         }
234 | 
235 |         if (!interferenceGraph.hasNode(v1) ||
236 |             !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v2)) {
237 |           // Skip nodes that were not added. They are globals and escaped
238 |           // locals. Also avoid merging a variable with itself.
239 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
240 |         }
241 | 
242 |         if (v1.getParentNode().getType() == Token.LP &&
243 |             v2.getParentNode().getType() == Token.LP) {
244 |           interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
245 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         // Go through every CFG node in the program and look at
249 |         // this variable pair. If they are both live at the same
250 |         // time, add an edge between them and continue to the next pair.
251 |         NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE:
252 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
253 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
254 |             continue NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE;
255 |           }
256 | 
257 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
258 |           // Check the live states and add edge when possible.
259 |           if ((state.getIn().isLive(v1) && state.getIn().isLive(v2)) ||
260 |               (state.getOut().isLive(v1) && state.getOut().isLive(v2))) {
261 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
262 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
263 |           }
264 |         }
265 | 
266 |         // v1 and v2 might not have an edge between them! woohoo. there's
267 |         // one last sanity check that we have to do: we have to check
268 |         // if there's a collision *within* the cfg node.
269 |         NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE:
270 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
271 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
272 |             continue NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE;
273 |           }
274 | 
275 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
276 |           boolean v1OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v1);
277 |           boolean v2OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v2);
278 |           CombinedLiveRangeChecker checker = new CombinedLiveRangeChecker(
279 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v1, v2OutLive ? null : v2),
280 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v2, v1OutLive ? null : v1));
281 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(
282 |               compiler,
283 |               cfgNode.getValue(),
284 |               checker);
285 |           if (checker.connectIfCrossed(interferenceGraph)) {
286 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
287 |           }
288 |         }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return interferenceGraph;
292 |   }

58 |       case Token.FOR:
59 |       case Token.WHILE:
60 |         tryMinimizeExits(
61 |             NodeUtil.getLoopCodeBlock(n), Token.CONTINUE, null);
62 |         break;
63 | 
64 |       case Token.DO:
65 |         tryMinimizeExits(
66 |             NodeUtil.getLoopCodeBlock(n), Token.CONTINUE, null);
67 | 
68 |         Node cond = NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n);
69 |         if (NodeUtil.getBooleanValue(cond) == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
70 |           // Normally, we wouldn't be able to optimize BREAKs inside a loop
71 |           // but as we know the condition will always false, we can treat them
72 |           // as we would a CONTINUE.
73 |           tryMinimizeExits(
74 |               n.getFirstChild(), Token.BREAK, null);
75 |         }
76 |         break;
77 | 
78 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
79 |         tryMinimizeExits(
80 |             n.getLastChild(), Token.RETURN, null);
81 |         break;
82 |     }
83 |   }

/**
   * ParamTypeExpressionAnnotation :=
   *     '{' OptionalParameterType '}' |
   *     '{' TopLevelTypeExpression '}' |
   *     '{' '...' TopLevelTypeExpression '}'
   *
   * OptionalParameterType :=
   *     TopLevelTypeExpression '='
   */
Method code:
1456 |   private Node parseParamTypeExpressionAnnotation(JsDocToken token) {
1457 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(token == JsDocToken.LC);
1458 | 
1459 |     skipEOLs();
1460 | 
1461 |     boolean restArg = false;
1462 |     token = next();
1463 |     if (token == JsDocToken.ELLIPSIS) {
1464 |       token = next();
1465 |       if (token == JsDocToken.RC) {
1466 |         // EMPTY represents the UNKNOWN type in the Type AST.
1467 |         return wrapNode(Token.ELLIPSIS, new Node(Token.EMPTY));
1468 |       }
1469 |       restArg = true;

1474 |       skipEOLs();
1475 |       if (restArg) {

1477 |       } else if (match(JsDocToken.EQUALS)) {

===== M0943 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 337-366
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured vairables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
337 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
338 |     switch (n.getType()) {
339 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
340 |       case Token.REGEXP:
341 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
342 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
343 |              child = child.getNext()) {
344 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
345 |             return false;
346 |           }
347 |         }
348 |         return true;
349 | 
350 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
351 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
352 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
353 |              child = child.getNext()) {
354 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
355 |             return false;
356 |           }
357 |         }
358 |         return true;
359 | 
360 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
361 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
362 | 
363 |       default:
364 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
365 |     }
366 |   }

===== M0954 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MaybeReachingVariableUse.computeMayUse(Node,Node,ReachingUses,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MaybeReachingVariableUse.java
Original range: 151-236
Documentation:

Method code:
151 |   private void computeMayUse(
152 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, ReachingUses output, boolean conditional) {
153 |     switch (n.getType()) {
154 | 
155 |       case Token.BLOCK:
156 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
157 |         return;
158 | 
159 |       case Token.NAME:
160 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
161 |         return;
162 | 
163 |       case Token.WHILE:
164 |       case Token.DO:
165 |       case Token.IF:
166 |         computeMayUse(
167 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
168 |         return;
169 | 
170 |       case Token.FOR:
171 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
172 |           computeMayUse(
173 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
174 |         } else {
175 |           // for(x in y) {...}
176 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
177 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
178 |           if (NodeUtil.isVar(lhs)) {
179 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
180 |           }
181 |           if (NodeUtil.isName(lhs) && !conditional) {
182 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
183 |           }
184 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
185 |         }
186 |         return;
187 | 
188 |       case Token.AND:
189 |       case Token.OR:
190 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
191 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
192 |         return;
193 | 
194 |       case Token.HOOK:
195 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
196 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
197 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
198 |         return;
199 | 
200 |       case Token.VAR:
201 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
202 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
203 | 
204 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
205 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
206 |           if (!conditional) {
207 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
208 |           }
209 |         }
210 |         return;
211 | 
212 |       default:
213 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isName(n.getFirstChild())) {
214 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
215 |           if (!conditional) {
216 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
217 |           }
218 | 
219 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
220 |           if (!NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
221 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
222 |           }
223 | 
224 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
225 |         } else {
226 |           /*
227 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
228 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
229 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
230 |            */
231 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
232 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
233 |           }
234 |         }
235 |     }
236 |   }

530 |       // function name (or else a semicolon will be inserted.)  If there's no
531 |       // function name, assume the paren was on the same line as the function.

===== M0971 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 675-772
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
675 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
676 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
677 |     /*
678 |      * This is the case where:
679 |      *
680 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
681 |      * the script.
682 |      *
683 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
684 |      * the caller of the function.
685 |      *
686 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
687 |      * back to the caller of the function.
688 |      *
689 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
690 |      * asked to traverse.
691 |      *
692 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
693 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
694 |      */
695 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
696 |     if (parent == null || parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION ||
697 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
698 |       return null;
699 |     }
700 | 
701 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
702 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
703 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
704 |       case Token.IF:
705 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
706 |       case Token.CASE:
707 |       case Token.DEFAULT:
708 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
709 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
710 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
711 |           if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.CASE) {
712 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
713 |           } else if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.DEFAULT) {
714 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
715 |           } else {
716 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
717 |           }
718 |         } else {
719 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
720 |         }
721 |         break;
722 |       case Token.FOR:
723 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
724 |           return parent;
725 |         } else {
726 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
727 |         }
728 |       case Token.WHILE:
729 |       case Token.DO:
730 |         return parent;
731 |       case Token.TRY:
732 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
733 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
734 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
735 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
736 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
737 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
738 |           }
739 |         // CATCH block.
740 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
741 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
742 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
743 |           } else {
744 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
745 |           }
746 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
747 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
748 |           if (cfa != null) {
749 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
750 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
751 |             }
752 |           }
753 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
754 |         }
755 |     }
756 | 
757 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
758 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
759 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
760 | 
761 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
762 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
763 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
764 |     }
765 | 
766 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
767 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
768 |     } else {
769 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transfered up the AST.
770 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |     }
772 |   }

/**
   * Try to remove useless assignments from a control flow graph that has been
   * annotated with liveness information.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal.
   * @param cfg The control flow graph of the program annotated with liveness
   *        information.
   */
Method code:
117 |   private void tryRemoveDeadAssignments(NodeTraversal t,
118 |       ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg) {
119 |     Iterable<DiGraphNode<Node, Branch>> nodes = cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes();
120 | 
121 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : nodes) {
122 |       FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state =
123 |           cfgNode.getAnnotation();
124 |       Node n = cfgNode.getValue();
125 |       if (n == null) {
126 |         continue;
127 |       }
128 |       switch (n.getType()) {
129 |         case Token.IF:
130 |         case Token.WHILE:
131 |         case Token.DO:
132 |           tryRemoveAssignment(t, NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), state);
133 |           continue;
134 |         case Token.FOR:
135 |           if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
136 |             tryRemoveAssignment(
137 |                 t, NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), state);
138 |           }
139 |           continue;
140 |         case Token.SWITCH:
141 |         case Token.CASE:
142 |         case Token.RETURN:
143 |           if (n.hasChildren()) {
144 |             tryRemoveAssignment(t, n.getFirstChild(), state);
145 |           }
146 |           continue;
147 |         // TODO(user): case Token.VAR: Remove var a=1;a=2;.....
148 |       }
149 | 
150 |       tryRemoveAssignment(t, n, state);
151 |     }
152 |   }

===== M0999 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.canInline(Reference,Reference,Reference)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 486-543
Documentation:
/**
     * @return true if the provided reference and declaration can be safely
     *         inlined according to our criteria
     */
Method code:
486 |     private boolean canInline(
487 |         Reference declaration,
488 |         Reference initialization,
489 |         Reference reference) {
490 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(declaration)
491 |           || !isValidInitialization(initialization)
492 |           || !isValidReference(reference)) {
493 |         return false;
494 |       }
495 | 
496 |       // If the value is read more than once, skip it.
497 |       // VAR declarations and EXPR_RESULT don't need the value, but other
498 |       // ASSIGN expressions parents do.
499 |       if (declaration != initialization &&
500 |           initialization.getGrandparent().getType() != Token.EXPR_RESULT) {
501 |         return false;
502 |       }
503 | 
504 |       // Be very conservative and do no cross control structures or
505 |       // scope boundaries
506 |       if (declaration.getBasicBlock() != initialization.getBasicBlock()
507 |           || declaration.getBasicBlock() != reference.getBasicBlock()) {
508 |         return false;
509 |       }
510 | 
511 |       // Do not inline into a call node. This would change
512 |       // the context in which it was being called. For example,
513 |       //   var a = b.c;
514 |       //   a();
515 |       // should not be inlined, because it calls a in the context of b
516 |       // rather than the context of the window.
517 |       //   var a = b.c;
518 |       //   f(a)
519 |       // is ok.
520 |       Node value = initialization.getAssignedValue();
521 |       Preconditions.checkState(value != null);
522 |       if (value.getType() == Token.GETPROP
523 |           && reference.getParent().getType() == Token.CALL
524 |           && reference.getParent().getFirstChild() == reference.getNameNode()) {
525 |         return false;
526 |       }
527 | 
528 |       // Bug 2388531: Don't inline subclass definitions into class defining
529 |       // calls as this confused class removing logic.
530 |       if (value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
531 |         Node callNode = reference.getParent();
532 |         if (reference.getParent().getType() == Token.CALL) {
533 |           SubclassRelationship relationship =
534 |               compiler.getCodingConvention().getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
535 |           if (relationship != null) {
536 |             return false;
537 |           }
538 |         }
539 |       }
540 | 
541 |       return canMoveAggressively(value) ||
542 |           canMoveModerately(initialization, reference);
543 |     }

Documentation:
/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
   * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.
   */
Method code:
1146 |   protected static int mergeLineCharNo(int lineno, int charno) {
1147 |     if (lineno < 0 || charno < 0) {
1148 |       return -1;
1149 |     } else if ((charno & ~COLUMN_MASK) != 0) {
1150 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | COLUMN_MASK;
1151 |     } else {
1152 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | (charno & COLUMN_MASK);
1153 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.BasicBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(BasicBlock)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 598-611
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether this block is guaranteed to begin executing before
     * the given block does.
     */
Method code:
598 |     boolean provablyExecutesBefore(BasicBlock thatBlock) {
599 |       // If thatBlock is a descendant of this block, and there are no hoisted
600 |       // blocks between them, then this block must start before thatBlock.
601 |       BasicBlock currentBlock;
602 |       for (currentBlock = thatBlock;
603 |            currentBlock != null && currentBlock != this;
604 |            currentBlock = currentBlock.getParent()) {
605 |         if (currentBlock.isHoisted) {
606 |           return false;
607 |         }
608 |       }
609 | 
610 |       return currentBlock == this;
611 |     }

===== M1035 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(n) && !NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (NodeUtil.isName(forVar)
85 |           && NodeUtil.isVar(n) && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // Ok, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.getType() == Token.FOR
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.EMPTY) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some Javascript parsers (such
101 |       // as the Playstation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

233 |   void addNumber(double x) {
234 |     // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of x- -4 as
235 |     // x--4 (which is a syntax error).
236 |     char prev = getLastChar();
237 |     if (x < 0 && prev == '-') {
238 |       add(" ");
239 |     }
240 | 
241 |     if ((long) x == x) {
242 |       long value = (long) x;
243 |       long mantissa = value;
244 |       int exp = 0;
245 |       if (Math.abs(x) >= 100) {
246 |         while (mantissa / 10 * Math.pow(10, exp + 1) == value) {
247 |           mantissa /= 10;
248 |           exp++;
249 |         }
250 |       }
251 |       if (exp > 2) {
252 |         add(Long.toString(mantissa) + "E" + Integer.toString(exp));
253 |       } else {
254 |         add(Long.toString(value));
255 |       }
256 |     } else {
257 |       add(String.valueOf(x));
258 |     }
259 |   }

892 |   static String jsString(String s, CharsetEncoder outputCharsetEncoder) {
893 |     int singleq = 0, doubleq = 0;
894 |

130 |     @Override
131 |     public int color() {
132 |       graph.clearNodeAnnotations();
133 |       List<GraphNode<N, E>> worklist = Lists.newArrayList(graph.getNodes());
134 | 
135 |       // Sort nodes by degree.
136 |       Collections.sort(worklist, new Comparator<GraphNode<N, E>>() {
137 |         @Override
138 |         public int compare(GraphNode<N, E> o1, GraphNode<N, E> o2) {
139 |           int result = graph.getWeight(o2.getValue())
140 |               - graph.getWeight(o1.getValue());
141 |           return result == 0 && tieBreaker != null ?
142 |               tieBreaker.compare(o1.getValue(), o2.getValue()) : result;
143 |         }
144 |       });
145 | 
146 |       // Idea: From the highest to lowest degree, assign any uncolored node with
147 |       // a unique color if none of its neighbor has been assigned that color.
148 |       int count = 0;
149 |       do {
150 |         Color color = new Color(count);
151 |         SubGraph<N, E> subgraph = graph.newSubGraph();
152 |         for (Iterator<GraphNode<N, E>> i = worklist.iterator(); i.hasNext();) {
153 |           GraphNode<N, E> node = i.next();
154 |           if (subgraph.isIndependentOf(node.getValue())) {
155 |             subgraph.addNode(node.getValue());
156 |             node.setAnnotation(color);
157 |             i.remove();
158 |           }
159 |         }
160 |         count++;
161 |       } while (!worklist.isEmpty());
162 |       @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
163 |       N[] map = (N[]) new Object[count];
164 |       colorToNodeMap = map;
165 |       return count;
166 |     }

===== M1127 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(Node,Node,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DeadAssignmentsElimination.java
Original range: 290-309
Documentation:
/**
   * Given a variable, node n in the tree and a sub-tree denoted by exprRoot as
   * the root, this function returns true if there exists a read of that
   * variable before a write to that variable that is on the right side of n.
   *
   * For example, suppose the node is x = 1:
   *
   * y = 1, x = 1; // false, there is no reads at all.
   * y = 1, x = 1, print(x) // true, there is a read right of n.
   * y = 1, x = 1, x = 2, print(x) // false, there is a read right of n but
   *                               // it is after a write.
   *
   * @param n The current node we should look at.
   * @param exprRoot The node
   */
Method code:
290 |   private boolean isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(
291 |       Node n, Node exprRoot, String variable) {
292 |     while (n != exprRoot) {
293 |       for(Node sibling = n.getNext(); sibling != null;
294 |           sibling = sibling.getNext()) {
295 |         if (!ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(sibling)) {
296 |           VariableLiveness state = isVariableReadBeforeKill(sibling, variable);
297 | 
298 |           // If we see a READ or KILL there is no need to continue.
299 |           if (state == VariableLiveness.READ) {
300 |             return true;
301 |           } else if (state == VariableLiveness.KILL) {
302 |             return false;
303 |           }
304 |         }
305 |       }
306 |       n = n.getParent();
307 |     }
308 |     return false;
309 |   }

Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
813 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
814 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
815 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
816 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
817 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunction(handler)) {
818 |           return;
819 |         }
820 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.getType() == Token.TRY);
821 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
822 | 
823 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
824 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
825 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
826 |           } else {
827 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
828 |           }
829 |         } else { // Has a catch.
830 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
831 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
832 |             return;
833 |           } else {
834 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
835 |           }
836 |         }
837 |         lastJump = handler;
838 |       }
839 |     }
840 |   }

/** Returns true if this node is equivalent semantically to another */

1595 |   public boolean isEquivalentTo(Node node) {
1596 |     if (type == Token.ARRAYLIT) {

1598 |         int[] indices1 = (int[]) getProp(Node.SKIP_INDEXES_PROP);
1599 |         int[] indices2 = (int[]) node.getProp(Node.SKIP_INDEXES_PROP);
1600 |         if (indices1 == null) {

1610 |             if (indices1[i] != indices2[i]) {
1611 |               return false;

1620 |       int post2 = node.getIntProp(INCRDECR_PROP);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReduceReturn(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 110-215
Documentation:
/**
   * Reduce "return undefined" or "return void 0" to simply "return".
   *
   * Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
110 |   private Node tryReduceReturn(Node n) {
111 |     Node result = n.getFirstChild();
112 | 
113 |     boolean possibleException = result != null &&
114 |         ControlFlowAnalysis.mayThrowException(result);
115 | 
116 |     // Try to use a substitute that with a break because it is shorter.
117 | 
118 |     // First lets pretend it is a break with no labels.
119 |     Node breakTarget = n;
120 |     boolean safe = true;
121 | 
122 |     for (;!ControlFlowAnalysis.isBreakTarget(breakTarget, null /* no label */);
123 |         breakTarget = breakTarget.getParent()) {
124 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunction(breakTarget) ||
125 |           breakTarget.getType() == Token.SCRIPT) {
126 | 
127 |           // We can switch the return to a break if the return value has
128 |           // side effect and it must encounter a finally.
129 | 
130 |           // example: return alert('a') -> finally { alert('b') } ->
131 |           //          return alert('a')
132 |           // prints a then b. If the first return is a break,
133 |           // it prints b then a.
134 |         safe = false;
135 |         break;
136 |       }
137 |     }
138 | 
139 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(breakTarget);
140 | 
141 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the break and return will
142 |     // also trigger all the finally blocks. However, the order of execution is
143 |     // slightly changed. Consider:
144 |     //
145 |     // return a() -> finally { b() } -> return a()
146 |     //
147 |     // which would call a() first. However, changing the first return to a
148 |     // break will result in calling b().
149 |     while (follow != null &&
150 |         NodeUtil.isTryFinallyNode(follow.getParent(), follow)) {
151 |       if (result != null &&
152 |           // TODO(user): Use the new side effects API for more accuracy.
153 |           (NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected(result) ||
154 |            NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(result))) {
155 |         safe = false;
156 |         break;
157 |       }
158 |       follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(follow);
159 |     }
160 | 
161 |     if (safe) {
162 |       if (follow == null) {
163 |         // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
164 |         // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
165 |         if (result == null) {
166 |           n.setType(Token.BREAK);
167 |           reportCodeChange();
168 |           return n;
169 |         }
170 | 
171 |       } else if (follow.getType() == Token.RETURN &&
172 |           (result == follow.getFirstChild() ||
173 |            (result != null && follow.hasChildren() &&
174 |             result.checkTreeEqualsSilent(follow.getFirstChild())) &&
175 |             ControlFlowAnalysis.getExceptionHandler(n) ==
176 |             ControlFlowAnalysis.getExceptionHandler(follow)
177 |            )) {
178 |         // When the follow is a return, if both doesn't return anything
179 |         // or both returns the same thing. This mean we can replace it with a
180 |         // break.
181 |         n.removeChildren();
182 |         n.setType(Token.BREAK);
183 |         reportCodeChange();
184 |         return n;
185 |       }
186 |       // If any of the above is executed, we must return because n is no longer
187 |       // a "return" node.
188 |     }
189 | 
190 |     // TODO(user): consider cases such as if (x) { return 1} return 1;
191 | 
192 |     if (result != null) {
193 |       switch (result.getType()) {
194 |         case Token.VOID:
195 |           Node operand = result.getFirstChild();
196 |           if (!mayHaveSideEffects(operand)) {
197 |             n.removeFirstChild();
198 |             reportCodeChange();
199 |           }
200 |           break;
201 |         case Token.NAME:
202 |           String name = result.getString();
203 |           if (name.equals("undefined")) {
204 |             n.removeFirstChild();
205 |             reportCodeChange();
206 |           }
207 |           break;
208 |         default:
209 |           //Do nothing
210 |             break;
211 |       }
212 |     }
213 | 
214 |     return n;
215 |   }

99 |         if (aliasDefinition.getParent().getType() == Token.VAR &&
100 |             aliasDefinition.getParent().hasOneChild()) {
101 |           aliasDefinition.getParent().detachFromParent();
102 |         } else {
103 |           aliasDefinition.detachFromParent();
104 |         }
105 |       }
106 | 
107 |       // Collapse the scopes.
108 |       for (Node scopeCall : traversal.getScopeCalls()) {
109 |         Node expressionWithScopeCall = scopeCall.getParent();
110 |         Node scopeClosureBlock = scopeCall.getLastChild().getLastChild();
111 |         scopeClosureBlock.detachFromParent();
112 |         expressionWithScopeCall.getParent().replaceChild(
113 |             expressionWithScopeCall,
114 |             scopeClosureBlock);
115 |         NodeUtil.tryMergeBlock(scopeClosureBlock);
116 |       }
117 | 
118 |       if (traversal.getAliasUsages().size() > 0 ||
119 |           traversal.getAliasDefinitions().size() > 0 ||
120 |           traversal.getScopeCalls().size() > 0) {
121 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
122 |       }
123 |     }
124 |   }

===== M1196 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runCallable(Callable<T>,boolean,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 553-604
Documentation:

Method code:
553 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
554 |   static <T> T runCallable(
555 |       final Callable<T> callable, boolean useLargeStackThread, boolean trace) {
556 | 
557 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the jscompiler overflows the stack when running on some
558 |     // large or complex js code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
559 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
560 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
561 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
562 | 
563 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = trace;
564 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
565 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
566 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
567 |       public void run() {
568 |         try {
569 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
570 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
571 |           }
572 |           result[0] = callable.call();
573 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
574 |           exception[0] = e;
575 |         } finally {
576 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
577 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
578 |           }
579 |         }
580 |       }
581 |     };
582 | 
583 |     if (useLargeStackThread) {
584 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
585 |       th.start();
586 |       while (true) {
587 |         try {
588 |           th.join();
589 |           break;
590 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
591 |           // ignore
592 |         }
593 |       }
594 |     } else {
595 |       runnable.run();
596 |     }
597 | 
598 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
599 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
600 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
601 |     }
602 | 
603 |     return (T) result[0];
604 |   }

Method code:
203 |   void addOp(String op, boolean binOp) {
204 |     maybeEndStatement();
205 | 
206 |     char first = op.charAt(0);
207 |     char prev = getLastChar();
208 | 
209 |     if ((first == '+' || first == '-') && prev == first) {
210 |       // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of
211 |       // things like "x + ++y" or "x++ + ++y"
212 |       append(" ");
213 |     } else if (Character.isLetter(first) &&
214 |                isWordChar(prev)) {
215 |       // Make sure there is a space after e.g. instanceof , typeof
216 |       append(" ");
217 |     } else if (prev == '-' && first == '>') {
218 |       // Make sure that we don't emit -->
219 |       append(" ");
220 |     }
221 | 
222 |     // Allow formating around the operator.
223 |     appendOp(op, binOp);
224 | 
225 |     // Line breaking after an operator is always safe. Line breaking before an
226 |     // operator on the other hand is not. We only line break after a bin op
227 |     // because it looks strange.
228 |     if (binOp) {
229 |       maybeCutLine();
230 |     }
231 |   }

/**
   * Traverses a function.
   */
Method code:
470 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {
471 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
472 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
473 | 
474 |     final Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
475 | 
476 |     boolean isFunctionExpression = (parent != null)
477 |         && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n);
478 | 
479 |     if (!isFunctionExpression) {
480 |       // Functions declarations are in the scope containing the declaration.
481 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
482 |     }
483 | 
484 |     curNode = n;
485 |     pushScope(n);
486 | 
487 |     if (isFunctionExpression) {
488 |       // Function expression names are only accessible within the function
489 |       // scope.
490 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
491 |     }
492 | 
493 |     final Node args = fnName.getNext();
494 |     final Node body = args.getNext();
495 | 
496 |     // Args
497 |     traverseBranch(args, n);
498 | 
499 |     // Body
500 |     Preconditions.checkState(body.getNext() == null &&
501 |             body.getType() == Token.BLOCK);
502 |     traverseBranch(body, n);
503 | 
504 |     popScope();
505 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 134-197
Documentation:

Method code:
134 |   @Override
135 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
136 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !NodeUtil.isName(n) ||
137 |         NodeUtil.isFunction(parent)) {
138 |       // Don't rename named functions.
139 |       return;
140 |     }
141 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
142 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
143 |     if (vNode == null) {
144 |       // This is not a local.
145 |       return;
146 |     }
147 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
148 | 
149 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
150 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
151 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
152 |         return;
153 |       }
154 | 
155 |       // Rename.
156 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
157 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
158 | 
159 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
160 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
161 |       }
162 |     } else {
163 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
164 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
165 |       // make this fast.
166 |       String pseudoName = null;
167 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
168 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
169 |         Var iVar = i.next();
170 | 
171 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
172 |         // and it is merged with the current coalscedVar.
173 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
174 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
175 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
176 |         }
177 |       }
178 | 
179 |       // Keep its original name.
180 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
181 |         return;
182 |       }
183 | 
184 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
185 | 
186 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
187 |         pseudoName += "$";
188 |       }
189 | 
190 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
191 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
192 | 
193 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
194 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessClosurePrimitives.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessClosurePrimitives.java
Original range: 144-229
Documentation:

Method code:
144 |   @Override
145 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
146 |     switch (n.getType()) {
147 |       case Token.CALL:
148 |         boolean isExpr = parent.getType() == Token.EXPR_RESULT;
149 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
150 |         if (left.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
151 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
152 |           if (name.getType() == Token.NAME &&
153 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
154 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
155 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
156 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
157 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
158 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
159 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
160 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
161 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
162 |               break;
163 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
164 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
165 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
166 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
167 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
168 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
169 |               if (arg.getType() == Token.STRING) {
170 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
171 |                 if (dot == -1) {
172 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
173 |                 } else {
174 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
175 |                 }
176 |               }
177 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
178 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
179 |               List<String> typeDecls =
180 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
181 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
182 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
183 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
184 |                 }
185 |               }
186 | 
187 |               // We can't modify parent, so just create a node that will
188 |               // get compiled out.
189 |               parent.replaceChild(n, Node.newNumber(0));
190 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
191 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
192 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
193 |             }
194 |           }
195 |         }
196 |         break;
197 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
198 |       case Token.NAME:
199 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
200 |         // object.
201 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
202 |         break;
203 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
204 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
205 |         // error. Hosited functions will explode if the're provided.
206 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&
207 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
208 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
209 |           ProvidedName pn = providedNames.get(name);
210 |           if (pn != null) {
211 |             compiler.report(t.makeError(n, FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_ERROR, name));
212 |           }
213 |         }
214 |         break;
215 | 
216 |       case Token.NEW:
217 |         trySimplifyNewDate(t, n, parent);
218 |         break;
219 | 
220 |       case Token.GETPROP:
221 |         if (n.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME &&
222 |             parent.getType() != Token.CALL &&
223 |             parent.getType() != Token.ASSIGN &&
224 |             "goog.base".equals(n.getQualifiedName())) {
225 |           reportBadBaseClassUse(t, n, "May only be called directly.");
226 |         }
227 |         break;
228 |     }
229 |   }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
1950 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
1951 |     char LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN = 0x7f;
1952 |     int len = s.length();
1953 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
1954 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
1955 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
1956 |         return false;
1957 |       }
1958 |     }
1959 |     return true;
1960 |   }

   * lattice. Do nothing if the variable name is one of the escaped variable.
   *

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.strEscape(String,char,String,String,String,CharsetEncoder)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 941-1002
Documentation:
/** Helper to escape javascript string as well as regular expression */
Method code:
941 |   static String strEscape(String s, char quote,
942 |                           String doublequoteEscape,
943 |                           String singlequoteEscape,
944 |                           String backslashEscape,
945 |                           CharsetEncoder outputCharsetEncoder) {
946 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(s.length() + 2);
947 |     sb.append(quote);
948 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
949 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
950 |       switch (c) {
951 |         case '\n': sb.append("\\n"); break;
952 |         case '\r': sb.append("\\r"); break;
953 |         case '\t': sb.append("\\t"); break;
954 |         case '\\': sb.append(backslashEscape); break;
955 |         case '\"': sb.append(doublequoteEscape); break;
956 |         case '\'': sb.append(singlequoteEscape); break;
957 |         case '>':                       // Break --> into --\> or ]]> into ]]\>
958 |           if (i >= 2 &&
959 |               ((s.charAt(i - 1) == '-' && s.charAt(i - 2) == '-') ||
960 |                (s.charAt(i - 1) == ']' && s.charAt(i - 2) == ']'))) {
961 |             sb.append("\\>");
962 |           } else {
963 |             sb.append(c);
964 |           }
965 |           break;
966 |         case '<':                       // Break </script into <\/script
967 |           final String END_SCRIPT = "/script";
968 |           if (s.regionMatches(true, i + 1, END_SCRIPT, 0,
969 |               END_SCRIPT.length())) {
970 |             sb.append("<\\");
971 |           } else {
972 |             sb.append(c);
973 |           }
974 |           break;
975 |         default:
976 |           // If we're given an outputCharsetEncoder, then check if the
977 |           //  character can be represented in this character set.
978 |           if (outputCharsetEncoder != null) {
979 |             if (outputCharsetEncoder.canEncode(c)) {
980 |               sb.append(c);
981 |             } else {
982 |               // Unicode-escape the character.
983 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
984 |             }
985 |           } else {
986 |             // No charsetEncoder provided - pass straight latin characters
987 |             // through, and escape the rest.  Doing the explicit character
988 |             // check is measurably faster than using the CharsetEncoder.
989 |             if (c > 0x1f && c <= 0x7f) {
990 |               sb.append(c);
991 |             } else {
992 |               // Other characters can be misinterpreted by some js parsers,
993 |               // or perhaps mangled by proxies along the way,
994 |               // so we play it safe and unicode escape them.
995 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
996 |             }
997 |           }
998 |       }
999 |     }
1000 |     sb.append(quote);
1001 |     return sb.toString();
1002 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessClosurePrimitives.ProvidedName.replace()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessClosurePrimitives.java
Original range: 749-811
Documentation:
/**
     * Replace the provide statement.
     *
     * If we're providing a name with no definition, then create one.
     * If we're providing a name with a duplicate definition, then make sure
     * that definition becomes a declaration.
     */
Method code:
749 |     void replace() {
750 |       if (firstNode == null) {
751 |         // Don't touch the base case ('goog').
752 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
753 |         return;
754 |       }
755 | 
756 |       // Handle the case where there is a duplicate definition for an explicitly
757 |       // provided symbol.
758 |       if (candidateDefinition != null && explicitNode != null) {
759 |         explicitNode.detachFromParent();
760 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
761 | 
762 |         // Does this need a VAR keyword?
763 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
764 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(candidateDefinition)) {
765 |           candidateDefinition.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_NAMESPACE, true);
766 |           Node assignNode = candidateDefinition.getFirstChild();
767 |           Node nameNode = assignNode.getFirstChild();
768 |           if (nameNode.getType() == Token.NAME) {
769 |             // Need to convert this assign to a var declaration.
770 |             Node valueNode = nameNode.getNext();
771 |             assignNode.removeChild(nameNode);
772 |             assignNode.removeChild(valueNode);
773 |             nameNode.addChildToFront(valueNode);
774 |             Node varNode = new Node(Token.VAR, nameNode);
775 |             varNode.copyInformationFrom(candidateDefinition);
776 |             candidateDefinition.getParent().replaceChild(
777 |                 candidateDefinition, varNode);
778 |             nameNode.setJSDocInfo(assignNode.getJSDocInfo());
779 |             compiler.reportCodeChange();
780 |             replacementNode = varNode;
781 |           }
782 |         }
783 |       } else {
784 |         // Handle the case where there's not a duplicate definition.
785 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();
786 |         if (firstModule == minimumModule) {
787 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);
788 |         } else {
789 |           // In this case, the name was implicitly provided by two independent
790 |           // modules. We need to move this code up to a common module.
791 |           int indexOfDot = namespace.lastIndexOf('.');
792 |           if (indexOfDot == -1) {
793 |             // Any old place is fine.
794 |             compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(minimumModule)
795 |                 .addChildToBack(replacementNode);
796 |           } else {
797 |             // Add it after the parent namespace.
798 |             ProvidedName parentName =
799 |                 providedNames.get(namespace.substring(0, indexOfDot));
800 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName);
801 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName.replacementNode);
802 |             parentName.replacementNode.getParent().addChildAfter(
803 |                 replacementNode, parentName.replacementNode);
804 |           }
805 |         }
806 |         if (explicitNode != null) {
807 |           explicitNode.detachFromParent();
808 |         }
809 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
810 |       }
811 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node)

Original range: 855-903

/**
   * Replaces a new Array or Object node with an object literal, unless the
   * call to Array or Object is to a local function with the same name.
   */
Method code:
855 |   private Node tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node n) {
856 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.getType() == Token.CALL
857 |         || n.getType() == Token.NEW);
858 | 
859 |     Node constructorNameNode = n.getFirstChild();
860 | 
861 |     Node newLiteralNode = null;
862 | 
863 |     // We require the AST to be normalized to ensure that, say,
864 |     // Object() really refers to the built-in Object constructor
865 |     // and not a user-defined constructor with the same name.
866 | 
867 |     if (isASTNormalized() && Token.NAME == constructorNameNode.getType()) {
868 | 
869 |       String className = constructorNameNode.getString();
870 | 
871 |       if ("RegExp".equals(className)) {
872 |         // "RegExp("boo", "g")" --> /boo/g
873 |         return tryFoldRegularExpressionConstructor(n);
874 |       } else {
875 |         boolean constructorHasArgs = constructorNameNode.getNext() != null;
876 | 
877 |         if ("Object".equals(className) && !constructorHasArgs) {
878 |           // "Object()" --> "{}"
879 |           newLiteralNode = new Node(Token.OBJECTLIT);
880 |         } else if ("Array".equals(className)) {
881 |           // "Array(arg0, arg1, ...)" --> "[arg0, arg1, ...]"
882 |           Node arg0 = constructorNameNode.getNext();
883 |           FoldArrayAction action = isSafeToFoldArrayConstructor(arg0);
884 | 
885 |           if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS ||
886 |               action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITHOUT_ARGS) {
887 |             newLiteralNode = new Node(Token.ARRAYLIT);
888 |             n.removeChildren();
889 |             if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS) {
890 |               newLiteralNode.addChildrenToFront(arg0);
891 |             }
892 |           }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType,JSType)

/**
   * A generic implementation meant to be used as a helper for common subtyping
   * cases.
   */
Method code:
842 |   static boolean isSubtype(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {
843 |     // unknown
844 |     if (thatType.isUnknownType()) {
845 |       return true;
846 |     }
847 |     // equality
848 |     if (thisType.isEquivalentTo(thatType)) {
849 |       return true;
850 |     }
851 |     // all type
852 |     if (thatType.isAllType()) {
853 |       return true;
854 |     }
855 |     // unions
856 |     if (thatType instanceof UnionType) {
857 |       UnionType union = (UnionType)thatType;
858 |       for (JSType element : union.alternates) {
859 |         if (thisType.isSubtype(element)) {
860 |           return true;
861 |         }
862 |       }
863 |     }
864 |     // named types
865 |     if (thatType instanceof NamedType) {
866 |       return thisType.isSubtype(((NamedType)thatType).getReferencedType());
867 |     }
868 |     return false;
869 |   }

/**
   * @return true if this node marks the start of a new basic block
   */
Method code:
167 |   private static boolean isBlockBoundary(Node n, Node parent) {
168 |     if (parent != null) {
169 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
170 |         case Token.DO:
171 |         case Token.FOR:
172 |         case Token.TRY:
173 |         case Token.WHILE:
174 |         case Token.WITH:
175 |           // NOTE: TRY has up to 3 child blocks:
176 |           // TRY
177 |           //   BLOCK
178 |           //   BLOCK
179 |           //     CATCH
180 |           //   BLOCK
181 |           // Note that there is an explcit CATCH token but no explicit
182 |           // FINALLY token. For simplicity, we consider each BLOCK
183 |           // a separate basic BLOCK.
184 |           return true;
185 |         case Token.AND:
186 |         case Token.HOOK:
187 |         case Token.IF:
188 |         case Token.OR:
189 |           // The first child of a conditional is not a boundary,
190 |           // but all the rest of the children are.
191 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
192 | 
193 |       }
194 |     }
195 | 
196 |     return n.getType() == Token.CASE;
197 |   }

326 |       if (NodeUtil.isLhs(n, n.getParent())) {
327 |         // The expression to which the assignment is made is evaluated before
328 |         // the RHS is evaluated (normal left to right evaluation) but the KILL
329 |         // occurs after the RHS is evaluated.
330 |         return VariableLiveness.KILL;
331 |       } else {
332 |         return VariableLiveness.READ;
333 |       }
334 |     }
335 | 
336 |     // Expressions are evaluated left-right, depth first.
337 |     for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
338 |         child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
339 |       if (!ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(child)) { // Not a FUNCTION
340 |         VariableLiveness state = isVariableReadBeforeKill(child, variable);
341 |         if (state != VariableLiveness.MAYBE_LIVE) {
342 |           return state;
343 |         }
344 |       }
345 |     }
346 |     return VariableLiveness.MAYBE_LIVE;
347 |   }

/**
   * Finds all defines, and creates a {@link DefineInfo} data structure for
   * each one.
   * @return A map of {@link DefineInfo} structures, keyed by name.
   */
Method code:
171 |   private Map<String, DefineInfo> collectDefines(Node root,
172 |       GlobalNamespace namespace) {
173 |     // Find all the global names with a @define annotation
174 |     List<Name> allDefines = Lists.newArrayList();
175 |     for (Name name : namespace.getNameIndex().values()) {
176 |       if (name.docInfo != null && name.docInfo.isDefine()) {
177 |         // Process defines should not depend on check types being enabled,
178 |         // so we look for the JSDoc instead of the inferred type.
179 |         if (isValidDefineType(name.docInfo.getType())) {
180 |           allDefines.add(name);
181 |         } else {
182 |           JSError error = JSError.make(
183 |               name.declaration.sourceName,
184 |               name.declaration.node,
185 |               INVALID_DEFINE_TYPE_ERROR);
186 |           compiler.report(error);
187 |         }
188 |       } else if (name.refs != null) {
189 |         for (Ref ref : name.refs) {
190 |           Node n = ref.node;
191 |           Node parent = ref.node.getParent();
192 |           JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
193 |           if (info == null &&
194 |               parent.getType() == Token.VAR && parent.hasOneChild()) {
195 |             info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
196 |           }
197 | 
198 |           if (info != null && info.isDefine()) {
199 |             allDefines.add(name);
200 |             break;
201 |           }
202 |         }
203 |       }
204 |     }
205 | 
206 |     CollectDefines pass = new CollectDefines(compiler, allDefines);
207 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, pass);
208 |     return pass.getAllDefines();
209 |   }
